The duties and responsibilities for a IT Project Manager (NETWORK/INFOSEC) GS-2210-13 generally include, but are not limited to, the following: Monitor infrastructure performance, availability, reliability, resiliency, operational readiness, and service dependencies; resolve complex operational issues.

Coordinate with budget, acquisition, contracting, program, and technical personnel to ensure effective management of IT resources. Develop network project plans, technical requirements, implementation strategies, schedules, milestones, and resource requirements.

Provide technical recommendations to contracting officials regarding contract administration, modifications, deliverable acceptance, schedule changes, and performance issues. Lead cross-functional teams of technical staff, program officials, contractors, vendors, and internal/external stakeholders.
To qualify for the position of IT Project Manager (NETWORK/INFOSEC), at GS-2210-13, you must meet the basic qualification requirements listed below. Basic Qualifications (2210 series): Please refer to the OPM IT Management Series 2210 Qualification Standard for the specific experience requirements for the GS-12 and above positions.

AND Specialized Experience: To qualify for the GS-13 grade level, you must have one (1) year of specialized experience equivalent to at least the GS-12 grade level in the Federal service, or comparable non-Federal experience.

Specialized experience is defined as experience performing the following duties: Participate in the planning execution and monitoring enterprise IT projects involving network services, information security, and/or telecommunications. You MUST meet all qualification requirements by the 09/04/2026 of this announcement.

Your resume must support your responses to the application questionnaire and the qualification requirements. Failure to do so may result in an ineligible rating. See the Required Documents section for important notes about what must be included in your resume.

After you submit this application, you will receive an e-mail informing you that a USA Hire assessment is required of you. You will have 48 hours from the closing date of this announcement 09/04/2026 to complete the assessment as this assessment is part of your application.

Clinical Services and Education The Anticoagulation Program Manger CPP have full responsibility to develop, organize, and manage patients diagnosed with conditions needing anticoagulation therapy and to coordinate further diagnostic assessment through appropriate professionals when there is question regarding the treatment diagnosis.

Serves as the facility Anticoagulation Program Manager. As the Formulary Manager, the CPP will serve as the primary prior authorization drug request reviewer.

Complete and document reviews in the Electronic Health Record in a timely manner (every effort will be made to complete reviews in no later than 96 hours of medication request) and include allergy assessment, ADR information, drug-drug and drug-food interaction potential, lab value assessment, elimination of duplicate/obsolete orders and appropriate drug conversions.

Clinical Pharmacy Services: Directly involved in the design, implementation and monitoring of therapeutic drug plans to achieve definite outcomes through direct interactions with patients and providers in assigned areas in pain as outlined in the individual's scope of practice.

Maintains an active scope of practice, serving as a pharmacist with advanced scope of practice within the ambulatory care through provision of patient care during new patient and follow up visits for chronic disease states.

Has expertise in the principles of clinical pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics and is knowledgeable and able to make dose adjustment recommendations based on objective laboratory findings.

Reviews patient medication regimens for clinical effectiveness, drug selection, dosing, contraindications, side effects, potential drug interactions, and therapeutic outcomes as required. Communicates findings with prescribers and provides appropriate alternatives to current treatment plans as needed.

Documents and ensure completion of clinical interventions, encounters, alerts and consults in CPRS in a timely and professional manner as appropriate.

Obtains medication histories from patients and summarizes significant findings in the medical record and/or to the provider as appropriate and is accountable for medication reconciliation according to facility policies.

Works with other Primary Care/Mental Health healthcare professionals (i.e.Physicians, Social Workers, Nurses, etc.) and assists in providing education and medication management to patients in both individual and group settings.

Education/Teaching/Training Directly involved in the training or support of pharmacy students, pharmacy residents, medical students, psychology interns, fellows and other graduate or post-graduate trainees, as appropriate.

Responsible for the self-development, mandatory training, and education necessary to maintain licensure, stay current with the practice of pharmacy and Joint Commission and OIG standards, and meet facility training requirements.

Provides leadership, guidance, and consultation to staff thorough the Medical Center and associated Community Based Outpatient Clinics as appropriate. Additional Role and Responsibilities Additional roles and responsibilities may be assigned as determined by the Chief, Pharmacy Service or the Associate Chief, Clinical Pharmacy Programs.

Outpatient Pharmacy Support Counsels patients appropriately regarding their medication and documents this in the notes section of CPRS. Serves as an authority on drug usage, interactions, over-dosages, and compliance to medical staff, nursing staff, technicians, and students.

Verifies electronic orders entered by the physician for accuracy while performing a prospective drug utilization evaluation considering drug-drug interactions, drug-allergy contraindications, drug-disease interactions, and dosage form.

Evaluates and utilizes professional judgment when determining service connection status, applicability of Agent Orange or combat veteran status, and co-pay status of outpatient prescriptions and resets incorrectly marked prescriptions appropriately Document information into VA Adverse Drug Event Reporting System (VA ADERS) and follows up as appropriate on unique cases as assigned.

Program Evaluation Assists in quality improvement and research initiatives and adds to the body of knowledge by participating in medical center and service process assessment and action teams and continually seeks to improve services.

Other Significant Responsibilities Serves on Medical Center or Healthcare System, VISN, and/or National VA committees or task forces as appointed or assigned by the immediate supervisor or Chief of the pharmacy service. Represents the Medical Center or Healthcare System at professional/program community group/events and committees.

Work Schedule: Monday-Friday, 8:00am-4:30pm Telework: Not Available Virtual: This is not a virtual position. Functional Statement #: 586450 Relocation/Recruitment Incentives: Not Authorized Permanent Change of Station (PCS): Not Authorized
Applicants pending the completion of educational or certification/licensure requirements may be referred and tentatively selected but may not be hired until all requirements are met. Basic Requirements: United States Citizenship: Non-citizens may only be appointed when it is not possible to recruit qualified citizens in accordance with VA Policy.

Education (1) Graduate of an Accreditation Council for Pharmacy Education (ACPE) accredited College or School of Pharmacy with a baccalaureate degree in pharmacy (BS Pharmacy) and/or a Doctor of Pharmacy (Pharm.D.) degree.

Verification of approved degree programs may be obtained from the Accreditation Council for Pharmacy Education, 20 North Clark Street, Suite 2500, Chicago, Illinois 60602-5109; phone: (312) 664-3575, or through their Web site at: http://www.acpe-accredit.org/.

(NOTE: Prior to 2005 ACPE accredited both baccalaureate and Doctor of Pharmacy terminal degree program.

Today the sole degree is Doctor of Pharmacy.) (2) Graduates of foreign pharmacy degree programs meet the educational requirement if the graduate is able to provide proof of achieving the Foreign Pharmacy Graduate Examination Commission (FPGEC) Certification, which includes passing the Foreign Pharmacy Graduate Equivalency Examination (FPGEE) and the Test of English as a Foreign Language Internet-Based Test (TOEFL iBT).

Licensure Full, current and unrestricted license to practice pharmacy in a State, Territory, Commonwealth of the United States (i.e., Puerto Rico), or the District of Columbia. The pharmacist must maintain current registration if this is a requirement for maintaining full, current, and unrestricted licensure.

A pharmacist who has, or has ever had, any license(s) revoked, suspended, denied, restricted, limited, or issued/placed in a probationary status may be appointed only in accordance with the provisions in VA Handbook 5005, Part II, Chapter 3, section B, paragraph 16. English Language Proficiency.

Pharmacists must be proficient in spoken and written English as required by 38 U.S.C. 7402(d), and 7407(d) Grade Determinations: GS-13 Experience. In addition to the GS-12 requirements, must have 1 year of experience equivalent to the next lower grade level. Assignments.

Candidates at this grade level are to be in one of the assignments listed below.

For all assignments above the full performance level, the higher level duties must consist of significant scope, administrative independence, complexity (difficulty) and range of variety as described in this standard at the specified grade level and be performed by the incumbent at least 25% of the time. Facility Program Manager.

Manages all aspects of a distinct program to include policy development, quality resources and specialty functions unique to the program to optimize cost effectiveness (budget) and patient outcomes.

Coordinates a single program area of a complex pharmacy operation, or multiple program areas within a facility to develop, organize, manage, and control complex pharmacy programs. Develops, organizes, coordinates and manages 6 single or multiple program areas within the medical facility; this may include a single program area at multiple facilities.

The Program Manager title is reserved for those individuals who have one or more of the following: supervisory responsibilities for various sections within Pharmacy Service; a complex program requiring coordination of multiple locations such as medical center care facilities, Community Based Outpatient Clinics (CBOCs), rural health, telemedicine, etc; specialized areas of a complex nature such as nuclear pharmacy, quality assurance, pharmacy informatics, clinical applications coordinator, Home Based Primary Care, pharmacoeconomist or liaison pharmacist duties requiring the coordination of processes with other medical facilities or VISNs Pharmacists assigned to this position must demonstrate the following KSAs: Ability to communicate orally and in writing to persuade and influence clinical and management decisions.

Expert understanding of regulatory and quality standards for their program area. Ability to solve problems, coordinate and organize responsibilities to maximize outcomes in their program area or area of clinical expertise. Expert knowledge of a specialized area of clinical pharmacy practice or specialty area of pharmacy.

Advanced skill in monitoring and assessing the outcome of drug therapies, including physical assessment and interpretation of laboratory and other diagnostic parameters.

Preferred Experience: PGY1 pharmacy residency or equivalent (3 years in practice area) Reference: For more information on this qualification standard, please visit https://www.va.gov/ohrm/QualificationStandards/. Physical Requirements: This position provides services to patients and their families.

Incumbents must be physically and mentally able to efficiently perform the essential functions of the position without hazard to themselves or others.

Normal work of the position requires visual acuity (with the ability to read typewritten characters without strain, corrective lenses permitted), keen hearing, clear distinctive speech, manual dexterity. This position may require reaching above shoulder-level height and requires potentially moderate levels of lifting and carrying (15-44 pounds).

This position requires long periods of sitting, standing and walking. The incumbent must be a mature, flexible, sensible individual capable of working effectively in stressful situations, able to shift priorities based on patient needs.

This position is for the Junction City, KS as their duty location. Provides comprehensive operational oversight and coordination for Junction City, Iola, and Lawrence VA Clinics, ensuring efficient day-to-day functioning and continuous improvement of clinical and administrative operations.

Evaluates outpatient service delivery models and develops recommendations to improve access, efficiency, and patient experience within assigned clinics and market areas.

Supports the delivery of high-quality, accessible, cost-effective health care services by coordinating resources, workflow processes, access initiatives, and support functions across multiple clinical disciplines to promote efficient clinic operations, timely access to care, and effective utilization of available resources. .

Leads and supports advanced analytical studies to evaluate clinical workload trends, patient flow, scheduling practices, and capacity management across assigned clinics. Uses data-driven methodologies to identify inefficiencies, forecast demand, and recommend organizational improvements.

Optimizes provider and care team scheduling by assessing clinic grid utilization, supply demand alignment, face to face and virtual visit distributions, staffing acuity, and clinical productivity indicators. Evaluates the impact of Community Care referrals on internal capacity, access to care, patient wait times, and care continuity.

Collaborates with clinical leaders to rebalance services between VA-delivered care, virtual modalities, and purchased care when appropriate.

Leads efforts to improve patient workflows by partnering with Primary Care, Mental Health, Specialty Care, and Nursing leadership to evaluate room utilization, care team composition, visit modality mix, appointment cycle times, and bottlenecks impacting throughput.

Develop operational solutions such as standardized workflows, enhanced scheduling procedures, process redesign, escalation pathways, and care coordination practices to enhance access and patient experience. Identifies and implements improvements to optimize clinic management processes and access strategies.

Standardizes, implements, and sustains key operational and business processes, including scheduling practices, to support efficient clinic operations and enhance the Veteran experience Incorporates remote healthcare considerations, including telehealth demand, virtual care readiness, space requirements for telehealth operations, and staffing support, to ensure seamless integration of virtual modalities into clinic operations.

Conducts analyses of telehealth utilization patterns, no show rates, broadband limitations, and patient adoption trends to support operational decision-making and service delivery planning.

Administers management reporting systems and dashboards to support data informed decision making related to organizational performance, staffing models, access metrics, quality indicators, and workload distribution.

Develops and coordinates quality assurance and performance improvement activities ensuring compliance with accrediting and regulatory bodies (e.g., Joint Commission, OIG, CARF). The HSS measures and assesses clinical business activities with an emphasis on improving clinical product line performance.

The HSS is responsible for regularly presenting key management indicators to the Executive Staff. Integrates administrative services-including Finance, HR, Acquisition, Facilities, Environmental of Care, and Health Administration Service-in support of clinic goals and market objectives.

Resolves complex operational, personnel, and cross service issues that impact patient care, staff performance, and organizational effectiveness. Provides leadership during change management initiatives, operational disruptions, and emergent contingencies that affect clinic operations.

The incumbent collaborates closely with key clinical leadership officials as an impartial facilitator in addressing disagreements related to scheduling practices, workload distribution, resource prioritization, and workflow redesign.

Employs conflict resolution strategies, mediation techniques, and interest-based problem solving to ensure concerns are addressed objectively, respectfully, and in alignment with EKHCS policies and organizational values.

Position Description/PD#: Health System Specialist - Project Manager/PD105350 Relocation/Recruitment Incentives: Not Authorized Permanent Change of Station (PCS): Not Authorized
To qualify for this position, applicants must meet all requirements by the closing date of this announcement, 09/04/2026. Time-In-Grade Requirement: Applicants who are current Federal employees and have held a GS grade any time in the past 52 weeks must also meet time-in-grade requirements by the closing date of this announcement.

For a GS-12 position you must have served 52 weeks at the GS-11. The grade may have been in any occupation, but must have been held in the Federal service. An SF-50 that shows your time-in-grade eligibility must be submitted with your application materials.

If the most recent SF-50 has an effective date within the past year, it may not clearly demonstrate you possess one-year time-in-grade, as required by the announcement. In this instance, you must provide an additional SF-50 that clearly demonstrates one-year time-in-grade.

Note: Time-In-Grade requirements also apply to former Federal employees applying for reinstatement as well as current employees applying for Veterans Employment Opportunities Act of 1998 (VEOA) appointment.

You may qualify based on your experience and/or education as described below: Individual Occupational Requirement (IOR): An IOR is a basic requirement that must be met in order to qualify for entry into this job series and it is something that can't be waived.

To qualify for the GS 0671 occupational series, applicants MUST possess one of the following: (for positions above GS-5): Progressively responsible analytical or administrative, or clinical management or supervisory experience in the health care field.

This work may have been performed in an operating health care facility or a higher organizational echelon with advisory or directional authority over such facilities.

Work must have involved a close working relationship with facility managers and analysis and/or coordination of administrative, clinical, or other service activities, and provided knowledge of the following: Missions, organizations, programs, and requirements of health care delivery systems; Regulations and standards of various regulatory and credentialing groups; and Government-wide, agency, and facility systems and requirements in various administrative areas such as budget, personnel, and procurement.

In addition to the individual occupational requirement, you must meet the specialized experience for the position as well:GS-12 Specialized Experience: You must have one year of specialized experience equivalent to at least the next lower grade GS-11 in the normal line of progression for the occupation in the organization.

Demonstrated mastery in applying analytical and evaluative methods and techniques to issues or studies concerning the efficiency and effectiveness of agency and program operations.

Expert knowledge of pertinent laws, regulations, policies and precedents, major issues, program goals and objectives, work processes, and administrative operations which affect the administration of GBO program and committee functions.

Mastery of VHA organization structure and operations to support VHA-wide assessments to improve the VHA system for health care. Expert knowledge of missions, organizations, programs, and requirements of health care delivery systems in general and in the country at large.

Excellent interpersonal skills to facilitate and coordinate vast needs for communications and information, between and among the stakeholders, including the Department, VHACO, VISNs, facilities and non-VA groups.

For more information on these qualification standards, please visit the United States Office of Personnel Management's website at https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/classification-qualifications/general-schedule-qualification-standards/.

Company Description
We are Olsson. We engineer and design solutions that improve the world around us. As a company, we promise to always be responsive, transparent, and focused on results – for our people, our clients, and our company.
We’re a people-centric firm, so it’s no surprise our greatest asset is our people. The impact this creates is an environment that encourages our people to grow and be creative with their talents. This approach builds a culture that is uniquely Olsson. It allows us to grow our people as we grow our business. This, in turn, creates a lasting impact on the world around us.
Job Description
At Olsson, we are passionate about improving communities through expert engineering and design. Our people are our greatest asset, and we are committed to creating an environment where you can grow, lead, and make an impact.
Our Data Center team delivers multidisciplinary engineering and design services for some of the world's most innovative companies. These projects represent some of the largest and most complex infrastructure developments in the country, creating opportunities to solve challenging technical problems, collaborate across disciplines, and shape the facilities that support global connectivity.
We are seeking a Lead Project Manager to lead multidisciplinary engineering design projects from early planning through final construction-ready documents. In this role, you will guide project teams, build strong client relationships, and help ensure the successful delivery of high-quality engineering solutions. You'll work alongside talented professionals across multiple disciplines while leading projects that support some of the industry's most advanced and fast-paced developments.

Lead project planning efforts, including defining project scope, milestones, schedules, deliverables, and project goals.
Manage project execution from concept design through final issued-for-construction documentation.
Coordinate multidisciplinary architecture and engineering teams to support the successful delivery of large-scale data center campuses.
Build and maintain strong relationships with clients, contractors, consultants, and project stakeholders through proactive communication and responsive service.
Facilitate project meetings, design reviews, and coordination sessions while driving accountability and progress across project teams.
Oversee the development and delivery of engineering and architectural design packages, including drawings, models, reports, calculations, and related project documentation.
Support quality management efforts by coordinating technical reviews and helping ensure the delivery of accurate, high-quality work.
Manage project budgets, monitor financial performance, track project profitability, and support contract administration activities.
Identify and proactively address project risks, challenges, and opportunities while keeping stakeholders informed and engaged.
Mentor and support team members while fostering collaboration, professional development, and project success.

Working collaboratively with others.
Having ownership in the work you do.
Using your talents to positively affect communities.

Bachelor's degree in Architecture, Engineering, Construction Management, or a related field. In lieu of a bachelor's degree, an associate degree with equivalent experience is required.
6+ years of experience within the Architecture, Engineering, and Construction (AEC) industry, with increasing project responsibilities.
2+ years of project management experience, preferably supporting multidisciplinary engineering or architectural projects.
Experience leading or coordinating large-scale industrial, mission-critical, or campus-style developments is beneficial.
Understanding of engineering and design processes, project delivery methods, contracts, budgeting, and project controls.
Ability to successfully manage project scope, schedules, budgets, and client expectations.
Strong leadership, communication, and relationship-building skills.
Proven problem-solving abilities with a proactive and solutions-focused mindset.
Commitment to exceptional client service and delivering quality work.

The typical annual salary range for this role is as listed below. Compensation may vary based on geographic location, experience, and qualifications. Employees in this role may be eligible for our performance‑based bonus and merit increases.

Additional Information
Olsson specializes in engineering and design, client advisory services, planning, field services, and environmental. Improving the world has been our mindset from the very beginning, back when Olsson first opened for business in 1956. And it will be our mindset for years to come.

Scale AI’s customer-facing engineering organization is one of the fastest-growing and most technically demanding in enterprise AI. Frontier Agentic Engineers sit at the center of our most strategic relationships; building, integrating, and troubleshooting directly with customers. Until now, there has been no dedicated enablement function to support them.
As Program Manager, Technical Enablement, you will build that function from the ground up. Your job is to make sure every engineer who joins this team ramps quickly and confidently, has access to an authoritative, maintained knowledge base they can actually trust, and stays sharp as Scale’s platform and product surface evolves.

You will own the full enablement lifecycle for customer-facing engineering, from day one onboarding through ongoing development, and you will be measured on ramp speed, knowledge base health, and the sustained readiness of the teams you support.
This role sits within the Enablement org and partners closely with FAE leadership, the broader Enablement team, and cross-functional stakeholders across Product, Engineering, Sales, and Delivery.

Build and Own Engineering Onboarding
Design and launch a structured, role-based onboarding program for new FAE hires, taking engineers from environment setup through meaningful technical contribution within their first 30 days.
Define fully ramped success criteria by role and communicate them clearly to new hires and their managers.
Own and Govern the Engineering Knowledge Base
Audit, consolidate, and maintain the authoritative technical knowledge base for customer-facing engineering, eliminating fragmentation, broken link chains, and stale documentation.
Establish a review cadence to keep content current as the platform evolves; tag owners and set expiration dates for key docs.
Create a clear document hierarchy so engineers always know which resources are canonical and which are deprecated.
Work with internal experts to surface the right documentation for the right audience, distinguishing what a new hire needs on Day 1 from what an established engineer needs to go deep.
Drive Ongoing Technical Development (Everboarding)
Develop and maintain a recurring enablement cadence (live sessions, async updates, release summaries) that keeps tenured engineers up to date on new capabilities, product changes, and evolving enterprise use cases.
Identify readiness gaps through feedback loops with managers and new hires, and develop targeted content to close them.
Stakeholder Collaboration & Program Management
Serve as the embedded enablement partner to FAE leadership, maintaining a close pulse on what the teams need as the business scales.
Collaborate with the broader Enablement team to adapt existing GTM enablement content for engineering audiences and bring engineering learnings back to the org.
Manage multiple concurrent programs with clear milestones, keeping stakeholders informed on roadmap progress and program effectiveness.
Report on program health and outcomes to engineering and Enablement leadership on an ongoing basis.

4+ years of professional experience in enablement, program management, technical training, or a closely related role.
2+ years of program management experience, with a track record of taking programs from zero to launched in a fast-moving environment.
Experience supporting technical teams, engineers, solutions engineers, or similar, at a B2B technology company.
Strong instincts for knowledge management: you’ve built or significantly improved a documentation system and have clear opinions on what makes them work.
Comfort navigating technical content: you don’t need to write code, but you can read a technical architecture doc, identify what’s outdated, and work with engineers to fix it.
Excellent written communication skills and a bias toward creating content that people actually use.
Proficiency with AI tools for content creation, summarization, and workflow automation.

Background in developer tools, AI/ML platforms, or technical product environments where the end user is an engineer or technical practitioner.
Experience building LMS-based learning paths or structured onboarding curricula for technical audiences.
Familiarity with tiered instructional design or adult learning principles applied to technical content.
Prior experience collaborating with Product, Engineering, or Delivery teams to extract and systematize institutional knowledge.
Experience in a high-growth, venture-backed environment where you’ve built programs from scratch without waiting for perfect infrastructure.
Compensation packages at Scale for eligible roles include base salary, equity, and benefits.

The range displayed on each job posting reflects the minimum and maximum target for new hire salaries for the position and may be inclusive of several career levels at Scale; it will be determined during the interview process based on work location and additional factors, including job-related skills, experience, qualifications, interview performance, and relevant education or training.

Scale employees in eligible roles are also granted equity based compensation, subject to Board of Director approval. Your recruiter can share more about the specific salary range for your preferred location during the hiring process, and confirm whether the hired role will be eligible for equity grant.

You'll also receive benefits including, but not limited to: comprehensive health, dental and vision coverage, retirement benefits, a learning and development stipend, and generous PTO. Additionally, this role may be eligible for additional benefits such as a commuter stipend.

HOK is a collective of future-forward thinkers and designers who are driven to face the critical challenges of our time. We are dedicated to improving people's lives, serving our clients and healing the planet. Together, we cultivate a culture of design excellence at the confluence of art and science, blending the power of creative expression with a clear sense of purpose.

In partnership with the Project Architect and Project Designer, accountable for project financial performance and team communication. Manages one or more projects during all phases of a project until completion. Directs employees and consultants at all levels to ensure that proper steps and procedures are taken and that work is completed as planned, budgeted, scheduled and in conformance with the design intent.

Leadership

Fosters and maintains a collaborative professional working relationship with the Project Leadership Team.
Participates on and/or leads multiple project teams as Project Manager.
Assists senior management in developing and validating project scope and fee, budget, and scope of services during the marketing and contract development process.
Assists in preparing project presentations. May participate and/or lead client presentations.
Consistently provides complete and timely communication of project information to and from clients and project team. Responsible for managing project using the Deltek Project Management system; completes work plans in Deltek; including identification of project team members, budget, consultants, schedule for completion, fees and costs as well as project change notices or other actions taking place on the assigned project.
Assists senior management in the preparation and execution of consultant contracts.
Assists with negotiating fees and contracts.
Ensures that budgets have been developed to provide for Quality Management Program through the life of the Project.
Incorporates Integrated Sustainable Design solutions into projects.
Takes personal responsibility for fostering a green workplace through sustainable work practices.
Fosters a commitment to external and internal client service.

Management

Works with Project Architect to avoid or eliminate conflicts in schedule due to the changes in various projects.
Plans, organizes and manages project. Provides on-going communication through team meetings/minutes/up-date memos to project team.
Communicates with consultants, contractors, sub-consultants and other disciplines to ensure effective communication.
Monitors construction administration during the construction phase
Develops and maintains positive relationships with clients and consultants.

Client Interface

Responsible for maintaining client relationships throughout project. Keeps client apprised of project progress on regular basis. Initiates and maintains contact with other key project individuals for clarification, coordination and negotiation of critical issues.
Consults with client to determine function and spatial requirements and prepares information regarding design, specifications, materials, color, equipment, estimated costs, and construction time. Plans layouts of projects and integrates engineering elements into unified design for client review and approval.

Business Development

Participates in developing annual business plan for the business unit.
Identifies new business opportunities while developing current client relationships. Listens for and seek out new projects which may exist or are being formulated.
Participates in selected marketing and business development opportunities.
Assists in development of fee proposals for marketing proposals.

Staff Development

Provides leadership including professional development coaching and mentoring staff.
Defines staff requirements for projects as needed or directed. Makes recommendations to senior management for staff promotions/terminations for project team and Architecture discipline. May participate in interviews and recruiting of professional staff.

Bachelor’s degree in architecture or equivalent in education or experience required. Master’s degree preferred.
5 years’ experience in architectural practice with management experience in all phases of projects through post-occupancy.
Licensed Architect with current registration in your region preferred, if licensure is offered in your region.

Travel may be required.
Overtime may be required.
The job duties and requirements that this document describes may be altered or supplemented at any time at the sole discretion of HOK.

Many of our roles require the use of specific software. Please refer to the Required and Preferred Software & Skills for details.

HOK invests in its people and communities, supporting both personal and professional growth through every stage of life. At HOK you’ll have a hybrid work environment, 10 paid holidays (including 2 floating holidays) and a minimum of 4 weeks of paid time off with a cash out option.

HOK offers comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage, free mental wellness resources, life and AD&D coverage and short and long-term disability benefits. HOK supports your growing family by offering 4 weeks of paid parental leave and fertility coverage.

HOK helps to fund your future financial needs with matching contributions to our 401(K) plan which includes a well-rounded investment menu as well as free guidance on retirement planning.

Wherever you are in your career, HOK provides opportunities to learn, develop and utilize your skills. Continued learning is promoted through financial support and study prep for licensure exams, CEU credit opportunities, mentorship programs, and paid professional memberships. To learn more about designing your career with HOK, explore our current job openings.

HOK is an EOE, including disability/vets.

Compensation is based on experience, qualifications, education and location. The reasonably expected salary range for this position is $120,000 to $150,000. Other compensation may include a discretionary bonus.

At ZGF, we are committed to the stewardship of people, place, and the environment. We thrive on multi-disciplinary engagement, practicing at the intersection of architecture, interiors, and urban design. As a Project Manager, you will…

Set direction, in collaboration with each project’s Partner/Principal-in-Charge, Design Partner, Senior Designer, and Project Architect, for the execution of project goals and objectives with project team and client, define of scope, identify items for investigation, and develop novel concepts and methods.

Optimize every team member’s opportunity for growth and professional development.
Display a passion for design excellence and exceptional project delivery while pursuing the highest value possible for our clients.

Fluidly move between project management tasks, production, and marketing as needed, dependent on office priorities.

Comfortable and effective in a leadership capacity to bring exceptional creativity and excellent technical knowledge to the delivery of high quality and complex healthcare projects.

Strong leadership and mentoring skills that can break down a bold vision into actionable steps, managing your team of architects to achieve extraordinary design solutions and outcomes.

Excellent team communication skills, design presentation, and storytelling skills.
Highly motivated, proactive, and passionate, and resilient.
Well-organized and detail oriented.
Ability to successfully navigate complex situations requiring diplomacy, interpersonal skills and judgement.

Experience in Design-Build, Design Bid Build, CM/GC and other forms of project delivery.

Professional architecture degree and a minimum of 8 years of experience in managing projects.

Senior Program Manager, Client Experience

Role: Senior Program Manager, Client Experience

Location: New York City (hybrid)

Type: Full-Time

Apply here

At Athletics, Client Experience is intentionally designed to build trust and drive outcomes for both our clients and the agency. We believe great creative work thrives when clarity, momentum, and thoughtful structure are considered.

We’re seeking a Senior Program Manager to lead complex branding and strategic initiatives for forward-thinking organizations. This role sits at the intersection of strategic account partnership and program delivery. You are responsible for translating brand and digital engagements into structured, scalable programs while shaping client relationships that deepen over time. You protect creative excellence by building the systems, alignment, and foresight that allow it to thrive.

This role is posted at the Senior Program Manager level. Depending on experience and demonstrated scope of ownership, we may consider candidates at the Program Manager level, with corresponding adjustments to title and compensation.

You will serve as the architect of the engagement. You bring order to ambiguity, stay calm in complexity, align stakeholders around clear outcomes, and anticipate friction before it slows momentum. You operate as both a strategic thought partner to clients and a delivery leader internally, ensuring programs are creatively ambitious, commercially sound, and operationally rigorous.

Senior Program Managers are not task managers. They are stewards of long-term partnerships, accountable for client success, project clarity, profitability, and identifying areas for program growth.

Program Leadership
Lead large, multi-disciplinary branding and digital projects. Define program architecture: scope, phasing, success metrics, and stakeholder alignment.
Elevate conversations beyond deliverables, helping clients clarify priorities, navigate tradeoffs, and make confident decisions.
Client Engagement & Partnership Development
Serve as a primary point of contact and trusted advisor. Design a Client Experience that is proactive, transparent, and insight-driven (not reactive or transactional).
Identify and shape natural growth opportunities grounded in client need and program evolution.
Delivery Excellence & Risk Management
Own end-to-end execution across scope, timeline, budget, and quality. Proactively identify risks, surface tensions early, and propose solutions before issues escalate.
Ensure work is delivered to brief, aligned to strategic intent, and executed with operational discipline.
Team Leadership & Cross-Functional Alignment
Partner closely with Strategy, Creative, Technology, and the Resourcing Director to assemble and support the right teams. Create clarity in roles, expectations, and decision-making authority.
Financial Accountability
Track and report on financial health across engagements. Forecast resource needs, manage profitability, and identify efficiencies across your programs.
Process Improvement
Help advance internal tools and systems to improve clarity, collaboration, and delivery. Bring a continuous improvement mindset to the team.
Mentorship & Leadership
Provide thoughtful guidance and leadership to junior team members, supporting growth while upholding standards of excellence. Model calm, decisive leadership in high-pressure moments.

Clients seek your perspective early, not just your updates.
Programs consistently meet or exceed project health expectations.
Teams describe your program plans as clear, decisive, and enabling.
You proactively identify risks (and potential solutions) before they become client-facing challenges.
Engagements evolve into long-term partnerships (when feasible).

5+ years of experience managing branding programs in a creative agency or consultancy environment.
Proven success leading complex, high-stakes projects from pitch through launch.
Fluency in brand strategy, visual identity, and digital product design/development processes.
Strong business acumen: able to forecast, scope, budget, and communicate with clarity and confidence.
Empathy and diplomacy: able to manage client relationships and internal dynamics with nuance. You’re calm under pressure and bring a positive mindset
Excellent written and verbal communication skills; you can lead a room or finesse a slide deck with ease.
Experience working and experimenting with both traditional project management best practice tools like Notion, Smartsheet, and similar, alongside rapidly evolving AI platforms
Bachelor’s degree required; project management certifications and/or advanced degrees are a plus.

Athletics is a brand innovation studio based in NYC, working with organizations at the forefront of culture, technology, and design. We are committed to building a diverse, equitable, and inclusive workplace where creativity thrives and careers grow.

This is a rare opportunity to shape the future of creative delivery at a growing studio—balancing structure with ambition, and process with possibility.

Athletics operates in a hybrid model, with employees working in-person from our studio in Brooklyn, NY a minimum of 2 days per week. Our model has flexibility for our team built-in, including fully remote options during the summer, plus remote work week allowances in the fall, winter, and spring. Candidates should be based in proximity to NYC and able to work in-person in accordance with our policy.

Base salary $90-120K, depending on experience and skillset. Benefits for full-time employees include participation in a value-sharing plan with bonus payouts; health insurance; 401k with guaranteed employee contribution; life insurance; generous paid time off; professional development budget; weekly team meals and in-office snacks; free Citibike memberships; + additional health and wellness perks.

Would you like to lead ambitious projects, take on responsibility, and work with a team to develop compelling solutions? Do you have experience in project management, the ability to keep track of the big picture, and a keen eye for quality? If so, we look forward to getting to know you.

C.F. Møller Architects is one of Scandinavia’s leading architectural firms and has been synonymous with award-winning architecture in the Nordic countries and around the world for over 100 years. Our work combines experience, innovation, and Nordic values to create architectural quality that meets both sustainable and aesthetic standards. In this way, we create solutions with lasting value—for clients, users, and society.

C.F. Møller Architects has also had a presence in Berlin for the past seven years. In our office, located on a bright top floor in Schöneberg between Gleisdreieckpark and the Neue Nationalgalerie, an international team of over 35 architects works on a wide variety of projects.

For our Berlin office, we are currently seeking experienced architects to lead challenging projects in Germany, particularly in the areas of office, administrative, cultural, research, and education buildings. You will become part of the multidisciplinary team at C.F. Møller Architects, where a passion for design, holistic thinking, and the commitment to turning creative ideas into compelling solutions shape our daily work.

You are an architect with extensive experience in project management and are familiar with the diverse requirements of complex construction projects—from conception through planning to completion. You are skilled at confidently integrating design, technical, economic, and organizational aspects.

You possess a strong architectural and technical understanding that enables you to confidently assess the quality of plans and develop compelling solutions to both design and structural challenges. Managing budgets, deadlines, and processes is just as much a part of your role as maintaining close coordination with senior management.

Your leadership skills are based on experience leading teams and projects, as well as on an empathetic, engaging, and clear communication style. When interacting with colleagues, clients, and specialist planners, you come across as confident, professional, and solution-oriented.

You bring five to seven years’ experience in project management in German-speaking countries, as well as in-depth knowledge of all project phases.

You combine a commitment to quality down to the last detail with a clear view of the bigger picture, and you stand out for your dedication, attention to detail, openness, team spirit and forward-thinking approach. Excellent communication skills and a good command of German and English are essential.

Proficiency in Revit/BIM, MS Office and Adobe CS rounds off your profile.

We offer you a permanent, full-time position with a salary commensurate with your experience and performance, as well as the opportunity to work independently and take on responsibility. As part of an international team of around 300 colleagues across eight locations, you will be introduced to the in-house standards of C.F. Møller Architects.

Your place of work is Berlin. In addition, you will occasionally travel to the sites of our construction projects and to our headquarters in Denmark.

We support your professional and personal development through internal seminars and regular participation in external training programs. You can expect a dedicated team characterized by open communication, mutual respect, and strong camaraderie.

Practical Information
Please submit your complete application materials in German or English via our career portal.

Your application should include a compelling portfolio, a cover letter, and a resume in table format specifying your available start date and salary expectations, as a PDF file no longer than 50 pages or 20 MB.

We work on a wide range of transportation projects, including local and State roadways, intersections, and interchanges, bicycle and pedestrian facilities, and other major infrastructure efforts throughout Idaho and the Inland and Pacific Northwest.

Our team supports projects from early planning and feasibility through design, permitting, and construction.

We collaborate closely with public agencies (local, state and federal), transit and port authorities, contractors, and fellow engineers to deliver thoughtful, sustainable solutions that improve mobility, restore natural systems, and strengthen the built environment.

Established in 2024 by engineers who call Northern Idaho home, KPFF’s Coeur d’Alene office is our newest (and one of our most exciting) additions! As we continue to expand our presence across the state, we’re seeking a Senior Transportation Engineer/Project Manager to contribute to the development of infrastructure projects and support the growth of our local practice. This role offers the opportunity to join a growing team early and play an integral part in shaping our work in the region.

Design a diverse array of transportation projects in a collaborative, multidisciplinary environment
Work on challenging and meaningful projects from concept through construction
Engage with clients and agency partners
Develop project management, leadership and entrepreneurial skills
Help grow our Idaho practice and shape the future of KPFF Coeur d’Alene

Experience working with or for Local Agencies or Highway Districts.

The Position
Roche Services & Solutions (RSS) aims at "transforming the way Roche operates.'' As a global organization of over 3,500 colleagues, we enable Roche to operate in a competitive and ever-changing business environment. We provide our partners with end-to-end business services and solutions, enabling them to focus on patient-centric activities.

Embracing a OneRoche mindset, we leverage our global network located in Budapest (Hungary), Riga (Latvia), Chennai & Hyderabad (India), San José (Costa Rica), Kuala Lumpur (Malaysia), and our other sites to remain customer-centric 24/7 and co-create solutions together.
The Opportunity
As Project Manager you will be part of the RSS Project Management organization and report to the Chapter Lead for Methodology Coaching . Are you a project management enthusiast and want to provide best in class project management services to partners across Roche? Then you are the candidate we are looking for.
In this role you will be responsible for successful Project Delivery using agile or traditional project management methodology. Your work will include but will not be limited to:
Engagement Delivery
Business Value & Success Factors: Understanding the business goals and value of the project to deliver defined organizational benefits, while ensuring critical success factors (reliability, compliance, efficiency, sustainability, time-to-value) are managed throughout the entire lifecycle.
Methodology & Execution: Using the appropriate methodology (Waterfall, Scrum, Kanban, SAFe) to manage dependencies and set clear priorities in a fast-paced environment.
Global Team Leadership: Leading or participating in global project teams by ensuring clear roles, responsibilities, and precise resource assignment to project plan deliverables.
Stakeholder & Change Management: Effectively managing stakeholders and understanding their organizations to establish key relationships, while applying organizational change management practices and ensuring effective project communication.
Facilitation & Coaching: Designing and leading workshops, acting as a proactive facilitator, and serving as a comfortable coach for project squads.
Planning & Risk Management: Generating, maintaining, and tracking an accurate and realistic project plan alongside a project risk and issue log, ensuring the project status remains timely and transparent.
Governance & Reporting: Preparing and presenting to relevant governance meetings as required by the chosen project methodology and good project management practice.
Financial Control: Tracking project financials and seeking governance approvals whenever needed.
Business Development: Contributing to business development opportunities where appropriate
Capability Building
Be an active member of the Methodology Coaching Chapter by
Continuously improve the project management capabilities, service offerings and community engagement leveraging latest developments and market dynamics
Supporting the development of training content and toolkits for our team
Actively managing your project management upskilling
Applying your learnings during engagements and sharing them with your chapter colleagues

You possess the following qualifications, experience and personal attributes
Appropriate university degree and 5+ years of project management related work experience
Deep understanding of project management fundamentals (Waterfall) and agile ways of working (Scrum, Kanban, SAFe), alongside related tracking and planning tools.
Experience in leading global/complex projects, organizing and optimizing resources and establishing clear priorities
Ability to motivate and lead a project team or team members if required
Excellent communication skills, with demonstrated proficiency in influencing, negotiating, and effective global collaboration.
Ability to effectively communicate across various levels of a complex, matrix organization. Ideally exposure to an additional field related to project management, such as project change management, business consulting, methodology coaching.
Experience in project management financials and resource management
In addition, the following skills will make you successful in your position and create the foundation for career growth at Roche:
Customer centricity
Collaborative ways of working
Presentation and influencing skills
Business acumen & systems thinking
Entrepreneurial and growth mindset
In Exchange we provide you with
Development opportunities: Roche is rich in learning resources. We provide constant development opportunities, free language courses & training, the possibility of international assignments, internal position changes and the chance to shape your own career.
Excellent benefits & flexibility: Roche Annual Bonus, Monthly transportation allowance, Home Office set - up equipment, Health Insurance, Life/Accident insurance, Full salary when on sick leave for the first 9 days, Eyeglasses settlement, One-time payment options for various events in the life e.g. wedding, childbirth, Service Awards: We value loyalty with additional holidays and bonus payment, Work in a hybrid model (2 days/week from the office)
A global diverse community , where we learn from each other. At Roche, we cooperate, debate, make decisions, celebrate successes and have fun as a team. Our leadership is very focused on people, creating a strong, inclusive culture, so you always have the chance to share your opinion.
Salary starts from 2800 EUR gross/monthly. Final salary depends on the successful candidate's level of experience, skills and qualifications.

A healthier future drives us to innovate. Together, more than 100’000 employees across the globe are dedicated to advance science, ensuring everyone has access to healthcare today and for generations to come.

Our efforts result in more than 26 million people treated with our medicines and over 30 billion tests conducted using our Diagnostics products. We empower each other to explore new possibilities, foster creativity, and keep our ambitions high, so we can deliver life-changing healthcare solutions that make a global impact.
Let’s build a healthier future, together.

Frontline work keeps the world running. Restaurants, hospitals, schools, nurseries, airlines, stores, emergency services. Together they employ 80% of the global workforce, over 3 billion people, and they're among the hardest businesses anywhere to run. By-the-minute scheduling, HR and payroll make them far more operationally complex than the average office, yet just 1% of venture funding has ever gone to software built for them.
Rising costs, wage increases, labour shortages and tighter regulation have made fixing that urgent. Sona is the AI-native workforce management platform for frontline organisations, with agents that match staffing to real demand and take the admin load off managers. That's a $500bn+ market the software industry has mostly walked past.
We've raised over $100M from N47, Felicis, Gradient and Northzone, signed more than 100 enterprise customers across the UK and US, and opened offices in London, New York, Austin and Lisbon. More on working at Sona here .

Continuously improve project processes and tools to enhance delivery speed, quality and customer satisfaction.

Proven success delivering enterprise software implementation projects on time, within budget and scope.
Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, including working with C-level executives.

Strategic thinker with strong risk management, planning and prioritisation capabilities.

Wir sind das weltweit führende Unternehmen im Bereich der Luftkeimsammlung. Seit mehr als 40 Jahren entwickeln wir Luftkeimsammler zur Bestimmung der mikrobiellen Verunreinigung von Luft. Du leitest Entwicklungsprojekte in unterschiedlicher Grösse von Kundenanforderungen bis zur Serienreife in enger Zusammenarbeit mit dem RnD Team und einem Netzwerk an externen Dienstleistern \- dabei trägst du die Kosten\- und Terminverantwortung
Du koordinierst die Zusammenarbeit mit unseren Kunden, Lieferanten und Entwicklungspartnern im In\- und Ausland

s.h: DEIN PROFIL? DU ÜBERZEUGST UNS MIT

Deinen Superkräften: Du kombinierst deine Kreativität mit technischem Wissen und behältst auch bei komplexen Projekten den Überblick

Structural Project Manager - Structures Practice
Los Angeles, CA
Full Time
Los Angeles Office
Experienced

You want to run projects. Not just work on them - actually own them, lead the team, build the client relationship, and put your name on the outcome.

Our Structures Practice is looking for a Structural Engineer with the technical chops and the people skills to do exactly that. If you've spent the last few years building your craft and you're ready to step into a project leadership role across commercial, multi-family, education, civic, or mixed-use work - let's talk.

Who We Are

Holmes US is an international structural engineering firm with offices up and down the West Coast and a home base that goes back over 65 years to New Zealand. We're part of the Holmes Group - 500+ people worldwide - which means you get the resources and technical depth of a global firm alongside the culture and relationships of a West Coast practice where people actually know each other.

Our Structures Practice takes on the kind of work that shapes how people experience their city: university buildings, multi-family housing, civic projects, commercial developments, and seismic retrofits of the buildings already standing. The variety is intentional - it keeps the work interesting and the skill set broad.

What You'll Actually Do

Lead structural engineering projects from concept through construction administration across commercial, multi-family, education, civic, or mixed-use building types
Own client relationships - managing scope, schedule, budget, and expectations with clarity and consistency
Develop technically rigorous structural solutions across concrete, steel, wood, and masonry
Direct, mentor, and develop a team of engineers and designers
Drive quality control and technical reviews on your projects
Contribute to business development through strong client relationships and repeat work
Collaborate across Holmes practice areas - and, when a project calls for it, across our international offices
4-8+ years of structural engineering experience in a consultancy setting

s.h: PE license required; SE license preferred or in active pursuit
s.t:
B.S. or M.S. in Civil / Structural Engineering
Seismic design experience - this is core to our practice, not a bonus
Demonstrated ability to manage projects and lead or mentor a team
Strong communication skills - you're as comfortable presenting to a client as you are reviewing calcs
Proficiency in ETABS, SAP2000, or RISA

Depending on your experience, this role will be placed at our Project Engineer or Senior Engineer level. What we're looking for in either case is someone ready to lead projects, not just contribute to them.

Why Holmes?

The breadth of our portfolio is a genuine advantage for your career. You're not going to spend five years on the same building type. You'll tackle seismic retrofits, new high-rises, school campuses, and mixed-use developments - often in the same year. That variety means you build a skill set that holds up over a long career.

We invest in our people seriously. Holmes University is our internal learning platform, giving you access to technical training and leadership development throughout your career. Senior engineers and principals here are genuinely available - mentorship isn't a line item in a brochure, it's how we actually operate. And when you need it, you have access to the technical depth of the Holmes network across New Zealand and Australia.

We also believe you follow your interests. There's a clear path to leadership and ownership at Holmes - and we'll be straight with you about what it looks like from where you're standing.

Work-Life Balance, and We Mean It

Our hybrid model is three days in the office - the rest is yours. We offer biannual profit share so you participate in the success you help create. And we've worked hard to build a culture where overtime is the exception, not the expectation. You'll do better work when you're not running on empty, and we structure the practice accordingly.

Hybrid work model
Comprehensive Medical, Dental, Vision, Life, AD&D, Short-term and Long-term Disability and other voluntary plans

Health Savings Account

Company sponsored events
Diversity / Inclusion programs and initiatives

$87,000 - $141,000+ depending on experience level and location, plus biannual profit share bonus potential. Salary is commensurate with experience, skills, and office location.

Our Commitment

At Holmes, we believe in building teams as diverse as the communities we serve. We provide equal support and opportunities for all our people to thrive, grow, and develop. Dream big - we'll help you get there.

Ready to lead projects that matter? Apply at www.holmes.us/careers.

Power Program Manager
· (194518)

At HDR, our employee-owners are fully engaged in creating a welcoming environment where each of us is valued and respected, a place where everyone is empowered to bring their authentic selves and novel ideas to work every day. As we foster a culture of inclusion throughout our company and within our communities, we constantly ask ourselves: What is our impact on the world?

Watch Our Story:' https://www.hdrinc.com/our-story'

Each and every role throughout our organization makes a difference in our ability to change the world for the better. Read further to learn how you could help make great things possible not only in your community, but around the world.

We believe electricity powers modern life. As part of our Power sector, you’ll help shape how electricity is generated, transmitted and delivered as global energy demands grow.

From massive data centers to modernizing transmission systems, our industry-recognized engineers and scientists have been at the forefront of grid transformation for more than a century. You’ll work side-by-side with these experts and contribute to reliable, resilient and sustainable power systems, helping communities thrive and industries expand.

This isn’t just a job, it’s a chance to drive infrastructure forward, power innovation and leave your mark on our energy future.

HDR is seeking a Power Program Manager to join our rapid-growth team to lead the planning and execution of programs and projects for our power clients. The successful candidate for this position will be a well-rounded, team-oriented individual with excellent communication skills who can deliver and execute infrastructure projects.

In this role, the Program Manager will lead a diverse, multidisciplinary team of technical and non-technical professionals to deliver power infrastructure projects.

The Program Manager will also serve as a trusted advisor to the client’s leadership team, providing guidance on delivery strategies, processes, and tools, and recommending effective approaches to program governance and team management.

Success in this role requires a strong focus on the client’s best interests and a commitment to HDR’s purpose: we do things right to make great things possible.

Lead multidisciplinary teams to deliver T&D, power generation, renewable energy, etc. projects to achieve strategic outcomes defined by clients.
Serve as primary point of contact for clients regarding scope, contract management, program performance, work planning, staffing, etc.
Advise clients on the technical, regulatory, strategic planning, delivery strategies, financial aspects of power programs.
Direct and manage the services provided by a program team comprised of HDR staff and subconsultants including engineering, project controls, routing and siting, environmental, real estate, strategic communication, data management etc. team based on the size, complexity, and phase of programs.
Assess staffing needs of programs and secure the resources required to deliver services specified in the contract scope with a focus on contract compliance. Promote team alignment on program mission and monitor team performance and establish a robust QA/QC program to meet client expectations.

As a Program Implementation Manager for Global Shared Services (GSS), you'll be responsible for managing the implementation of process improvement, automation, business expansion and/or GSS operational projects; aligned with team goals while working independently and seeking guidance as needed.

Program & Project Ownership
Manage the implementation of process improvement, automation, business expansion and GSS operational projects while meeting timelines and minimizing disruption to partner and engineering teams. Establish and track program milestones and deliverables, proactively mitigating risks throughout the project lifecycle.

Partner with process experts to identify inefficiencies and deploy solutions targeting efficiency gains, including buffer time and planning for unexpected challenges to ensure dependencies remain intact.
Oversee roll-out processes including UAT and pilots, then manage post-launch adoption tracking and reporting. Analyze data to make educated decisions while building implementation plans using different mechanisms and tools to showcase implementation timelines, phases, and milestones. Prepare executive documentation including PFAQs, narratives, and project updates using Amazon's writing guidelines for senior leadership.
Partner Coordination and Forecast Alignment
Build and maintain strong relationships with cross-functional teams to support operational readiness, ensuring the right people are part of conversations. Work with stakeholders and partners to validate forecasts, identify new volume opportunities, and secure resources while setting project priorities and milestones. Identify stakeholder needs for business expansion opportunities and serve as the first point of contact for GSS-related questions and topics.
Maintain recurrent connections to showcase GSS support and capture feedback, with cadence varying per region depending on the number of services GSS supports. Capture process gaps and process-level escalations from a partner standpoint, working backwards with GSS Ops. Enable alignment between GSS Ops leaders and Sports GSS partners while sharing support best practices among regions. Lock agreement on quarterly forecasts and support adjusting forecast expectations.
Strategic Execution & Decision Making
Understand relevant business requirements, goals, and interdependencies in your program area. Help GSS and Tech teams make trade-offs considering GSS goals, compliance, process workflow dependencies, and quality. Drive crisp and timely decisions, clear blockers, and escalate appropriately when needed.
Recognize when proposed ideas are too complex or risky and arrange additional stakeholder reviews. Prevent or mitigate consequences of poor business decisions. Determine if success metrics are in place; if not, work to define them.
Program Communication & Documentation
Own all program communication across stakeholders, communicating effectively with various audiences including senior leadership. Provide clear status updates and maintain transparency throughout project lifecycles. Foster collaboration across teams and organizations while sharing best practices and learnings.

· 3+ years of driving end to end delivery, and communicating results to senior leadership experience
· 3+ years of driving process improvements experience
· Experience in stakeholder management, dealing with multiple stakeholders at varied levels of the organization

About Anthropic
Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

Anthropic is bringing data center capacity online faster than the industry has ever attempted, and the owner-furnished equipment (OFE) that makes a site live — switchgear, transformers, UPS, generators, busway, PDUs, chillers, CDUs, air handlers, dry coolers, pumps and piping skids — is long-lead, high-value, and sits squarely on the construction critical path. When a transformer slips three weeks at the factory, a data hall slips three weeks at the site.
We're hiring a Supply Chain Delivery Manager to own that equipment from purchase order to dock.

You will be the site-facing supply chain lead for a regional portfolio of data center projects: tracking every OFE line item against the construction schedule, running factory and logistics escalations with OEMs, holding suppliers and general contractors accountable for delivery performance, and giving leadership a clear, converged picture of delivery risk across the portfolio.

Your job is to make sure equipment production and delivery are never the reason a site misses its ready-for-service date.
This is a senior individual-contributor role on the Compute DC Infrastructure team, working daily with Construction, Electrical and Mechanical Engineering, Strategic Sourcing, Commissioning, and our general contractors and OEMs. It is not a category-management or negotiation role — Sourcing owns supplier strategy and commercial terms — and it is not a people-management role. The emphasis is execution: schedules, escalations, logistics, and site readiness.

Delivery planning and schedule integration
Own the end-to-end OFE delivery plan for each site in your portfolio: order placement, engineering submittal/approval milestones, production slots, FAT dates, ship dates, and required-on-site (ROS) dates, integrated with the GC's construction schedule.
Engage during preconstruction with Construction, Engineering, and the GC to set OFE delivery expectations, sequence equipment arrivals to the build, and identify schedule risk before POs are cut.
Lead OFE kickoff meetings at the site level with the GC and internal construction teams, establishing points of contact, delivery windows, receiving requirements, and escalation paths.
Maintain the single source of truth for OFE status across the portfolio — a live tracker of every line item, its milestone dates, and its risk rating.
Supplier execution and escalation
Run weekly delivery cadences with OEMs and integrators on open orders; verify production progress against committed slots rather than accepting reported dates at face value.
Act as the primary escalation point for factory slips, component shortages, FAT failures, and shipping delays; drive recovery plans (expedites, partial ships, resequencing, alternate sources) with Sourcing and Engineering.
Partner with Sourcing on corporate-level supplier escalations, bringing site-level schedule intelligence to commercial conversations.
Hold GC OFCI teams accountable for receiving, storage, and installation-readiness performance; manage the change/claim process when delivery issues affect the GC's schedule.
Logistics and site readiness
Plan and coordinate transportation for oversize/overweight and high-value equipment — carrier selection, route surveys, permits, crane and rigging coordination — with our logistics partners and the GC.
Manage laydown, staging, and interim storage decisions when site readiness and equipment arrival diverge; coordinate with Quality and Commissioning on receiving inspection and storage/preservation requirements.
Ensure equipment arrives complete — accessories, spares, documentation, and vendor startup support scheduled — so installation and commissioning are not delayed by missing pieces.
Risk management and reporting
Identify, triage, and report delivery risks across the portfolio; propose solutions and drive decisions to protect capacity milestones.
Establish and lead recurring Capacity Delivery Reviews giving leadership converged visibility into OFE delivery status and risk by site and by equipment category.
Track delivery KPIs — on-time-to-ROS, schedule drift by supplier and category, escalation cycle time, expedite spend — and use them to surface systemic issues.
Feed lessons learned back into Sourcing (lead-time assumptions, contract delivery terms, buffer strategy) and Construction (ROS sequencing) to improve the next program.

8–12+ years in supply chain delivery, equipment expediting, construction management, or infrastructure program management on large-scale, schedule-driven construction programs.
Hands-on experience delivering power and/or cooling equipment for mission-critical facilities — transformers, switchgear, generators, UPS, busway, chillers, CDUs, air handlers — and familiarity with how those OEMs actually build and ship.
You've managed cross-functional escalations across construction teams, suppliers, and internal partners, and you know when to expedite, when to resequence, and when to escalate commercially.
Comfortable reading and influencing construction schedules (P6 or MS Project) and tying equipment milestones to them.
Strong written and verbal communication — you can turn a messy delivery problem into a one-page recommendation for leadership.
Data-fluent: you build and maintain trackers and dashboards, and you'd rather look at the numbers than trust a status email.
