Global Security plays a critical role in protecting Axon's people, facilities, operations, and reputation. As the Crisis Management Program Manager, you will build and lead the programs that enable the organization to prepare for, respond to, and recover from disruptive events.
Serving as the operational heartbeat and connective tissue across Global Security and key business partners; including Legal, HR, Workplace, Communications, IT, Manufacturing, and Executive Leadership, you will establish the frameworks, governance, and relationships that transform crisis management from a reactive function into a strategic enterprise capability.
This is a unique opportunity to build a program from the ground up, influence executive decision-making, and help shape the future of Global Security at one of the world's most innovative technology companies.

Build Axon's Preparedness Program
This role offers a unique opportunity to build a capability that will shape how Axon prepares for and responds to critical events around the world.

Working across Global Security and key business partners, you will design and mature the frameworks, governance, and operational standards that enable coordinated, confident decision-making when it matters most.

Success in this role will be measured not only by how effectively crises are managed, but by how well the organization is prepared before they occur.

Develop and execute the strategic roadmap for Axon's Crisis Management Program, ensuring it evolves alongside the company's global growth and operational complexity.
Design and maintain enterprise crisis management frameworks, governance, standards, and response methodologies that promote consistency across the organization.
Build and continuously refine crisis playbooks, decision support tools, and operational procedures that enable rapid, coordinated responses to a broad range of scenarios.
Champion a culture of preparedness by establishing sustainable processes that improve organizational readiness and strengthen enterprise resilience over time.
Lead Enterprise Crisis Coordination
When critical events occur, effective coordination becomes just as important as the response itself. In this role, you will provide the structure, leadership, and operational discipline that enable cross-functional teams to respond as one. By establishing clear decision-making frameworks, escalation protocols, and communication pathways, you will help ensure the right people are engaged at the right time with the information they need to make informed decisions.
Working alongside the GSOC, Physical Security, Threat Intelligence, Workplace, HR, Legal, Communications, IT, Manufacturing, and Executive Leadership, you will help orchestrate coordinated responses that minimize operational disruption, protect our people, and strengthen confidence across the organization.

Lead the coordination of cross-functional crisis response activities during significant security incidents and disruptive events.
Develop and maintain crisis activation procedures, escalation matrices, and decision-support frameworks that enable timely, consistent responses.
Facilitate Crisis Management Team (CMT) meetings, ensuring clear accountability, actionable decisions, and effective follow-through.
Prepare executive situation reports and operational updates that provide leaders with timely, accurate, and actionable information.
Coordinate post-incident reviews, capturing lessons learned and driving measurable improvements across the Crisis Management Program.
Strengthen Executive Decision-Making
During rapidly evolving situations, timely information and thoughtful coordination can significantly influence business outcomes. In this role, you will help transform complex, fast-moving events into clear, actionable intelligence that enables leaders to make informed decisions with confidence.

Working closely with the Crisis Management Team (CMT), GSOC, Threat Intelligence, and executive stakeholders, you will ensure decision-makers have the right information, at the right time, in the right format.

Develop executive briefing templates, situation reports, and decision-support tools that provide clarity during complex events.
Coordinate executive notification and escalation processes for significant incidents affecting people, operations, facilities, or reputation.
Partner with Global Security leadership to ensure executive communications remain timely, accurate, and aligned throughout an incident.
Support executive travel, strategic events, and other high-profile activities by integrating preparedness planning into broader security operations.
Continuously improve executive crisis support processes based on lessons learned and evolving business needs.
Build Trusted Partnerships Across Axon
Effective crisis management begins long before an incident occurs. Success in this role will depend on your ability to build trusted relationships across the organization, creating alignment before critical decisions need to be made. You'll become a recognized partner to leaders throughout Axon, helping departments understand how preparedness strengthens business continuity, supports operational excellence, and enables the company to respond with confidence during times of uncertainty.
Through collaboration, influence, and credibility, you'll strengthen Global Security's position as a trusted business partner while fostering a shared culture of preparedness across the enterprise.

Build trusted partnerships with leaders across Legal, HR, Workplace, IT, Manufacturing, Communications, GRC, Physical Security, GSOC, Threat Intelligence, and other business functions.
Facilitate cross-functional planning sessions that align roles, responsibilities, and response expectations before incidents occur.
Serve as the primary liaison for enterprise crisis preparedness initiatives, ensuring stakeholders remain informed, engaged, and aligned.
Promote preparedness through education, consultation, and relationship-building across the organization.
Represent Global Security in cross-functional meetings, projects, and strategic initiatives where crisis preparedness and organizational resilience are key considerations.
Advance Preparedness Through Technology & Innovation
Technology plays a critical role in enabling effective crisis management, but its true value lies in how it simplifies decision-making, strengthens situational awareness, and enhances organizational preparedness. In this role, you will continuously evaluate and improve the tools, processes, and technologies that support Axon's Crisis Management Program, ensuring they evolve alongside the company's growth and operational needs.

Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through national Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; community; student; social).

L'Unité organisation territoriale (UOT) de la Direction générale de la cohésion sociale (DGCS), contribue à la réflexion et au pilotage de l'organisation des prestations sociales sur le territoire cantonal.

Elle analyse les besoins des différentes régions, coordonne les acteurs concernés et accompagne la mise en œuvre et l'évolution des dispositifs sociaux, en veillant à leur cohérence et à leur accessibilité pour la population.

Elle a également pour mission d'assurer une vision cohérente transverse pour le parc immobilier subventionné par la DGCS qui comprend notamment l'hébergement médico-social (EMS, EPSM, ESE) et les ateliers à vocation productive, soit environ 400 bâtiments gérés par 250 partenaires.
Afin de mener un projet ambitieux visant à établir une stratégie pour la mise aux normes énergétiques et d'adaptation aux conséquences du réchauffement climatique du parc immobilier de la structure socio-sanitaire, l'Unité organisation territoriale (UOT) recherche **un·e Chef·fe de projet Plan climat.**

Das Bundesamt für Statistik engagiert sich im Rahmen der internationalen Zusammenarbeit für die Weiterentwicklung nachhaltiger Daten- und Statistiksysteme. Mit seinem Engagement unterstützt das BFS die Umsetzung der Agenda 2030 für nachhaltige Entwicklung und trägt insbesondere zur Stärkung datenbasierter Entscheidungsgrundlagen für die Erreichung der Ziele für nachhaltige Entwicklung (SDGs) bei.

The United States Space Force (USSF) Combat Forces Command (CFC) 13th Space Warning Squadron (13 SWS) at Clear Space Force Station, Alaska is searching for a Budget Analyst / Program Manager (NH-0301-03, GS 12/13 equivalent).

The ideal candidate is an agile, results-oriented financial and administrative professional with a proven track record of managing complex budgetary and resource allocation functions.

They possess deep expertise in the formulation, execution, and analysis of substantive program budgets, serving as a trusted strategic advisor to commanders and senior leadership.

Beyond financial acumen, the ideal candidate is a versatile leader capable of flexibly directing, managing, and adapting overarching administrative, personnel, and manpower support programs to meet the evolving operational needs of the installation.

Description: The employee carries out recurring assignments independently and conducts successive activities with objectives and priorities identified by the supervisor or team leader. Assistance is given on new or unusual projects or situations. The finished work is reviewed to ensure accuracy and technical soundness.

This position involves 51% or more of time in direct support of budget analysis and financial acquisition positions. Advises the installation commander on all budgetary, financial, and overarching resource management matters.

Executes the commander's vision on resource allocation in support of mission and installation operations, maintenance, and sustainment. Directly assists the commander in the flexible management of all administrative support program functions, anticipating organizational needs.

Administer programs serves as the primary source of information and proposes alternate approaches to management to more efficiently operate programs and comply with higher-echelon policies.

Assists the commander in accomplishing all necessary internal operations, to include administrative training, security, development of organizational operating instructions and regulations, and personnel assistance. Serves as the resident subject matter expert for all mandated administrative support and resource management programs.

Ensures unit program compliance with regulations, laws, policies, and squadron commander directives.

To maintain maximum operational flexibility, responsibilities include, but are not limited to: task management, cybersecurity liaison (CL), Government Travel Card (GTC) program, Unit Deployment Manager (UDM), Defense Travel System (DTS) administrator, Drug Demand Reduction Program (DDRP), health care program, fitness program, Government Purchase Card (GPC) program, safety program, Automated Data Processing Equipment (ADPE) accounts, security program, supply program, civilian timecard program, and unit recognition program.

Assists in planning, administering, and monitoring manpower resource requirements. Serves as the point of contact for both civilian and military position utilization. Maintains manpower manning documents. Reviews requests for revised manpower authorizations and makes recommendations for approval or disapproval as required.

Receives changes to the Unit Manning Document (UMD), notifies appropriate officials, and follows up with appropriate action. Performs budget formulation work, including the preparation of detailed analyses of annual and/or multi-year budget estimates for assigned organizations/programs into a consolidated budget request.

Performs budget analysis, execution, and administration involving the monitoring of obligations incurred and the actual expenditures of a budget with different sources and types of funding. This includes direct annual, multi-year, and no-year appropriations, apportionments, allotments, inter-agency funds transfers, and refunds.

Key Skills and Abilities: Knowledge of commonly used budgetary methods, practices, procedures, regulations, policies, and processes. Knowledge of missions, functions, goals, objectives, work processes, and sources of funding pertinent to installation programs/organizations.

Knowledge of automated data processing concepts and systems capabilities to accomplish budget/funding tasks. Knowledge of administrative, personnel, and manpower regulations, operating procedures, and policies to support the organizational mission.

Skill in the application of methods and techniques (e.g., cost-benefit analysis, ZBB, amortization) to analyze and evaluate the effects of changes in program plans and funding. Skill in formulating, justifying, and/or executing assigned budgets/programs.

Information Management - Identifies a need for and knows where or how to gather information; organizes and maintains information or information management systems.

Interpersonal Skills - Shows understanding, friendliness, courtesy, tact, empathy, concern, and politeness to others; develops and maintains effective relationships with others; may include effectively dealing with individuals who are difficult, hostile, or distressed; relates well to people from varied backgrounds and different situations.

IT systems, expertise, and experience are central to Asana's mission of helping teams work together effortlessly. As an IT Technical Program Manager, you'll be a force multiplier across IT and Asana's cross-functional business partners.

You will drive outcomes, programs, and operational rhythms that make IT highly effective and visible outside its own walls. IT TPM work is rarely IT-only: you'll be leading projects, programs, and processes that reach into Security, Product, Workplace, PeopleOps, Legal, and other business lines as a matter of course, not exception.
You'll join the team as a TPM, reporting to the IT TPM function lead, and take ownership of a dynamic portfolio of IT programs and projects. This is a high-autonomy role for someone who wants real ownership early: you'll be trusted to run point on your portfolio while helping shape how the broader IT TPM function operates.
This role is based in our San Francisco office with an office-centric hybrid schedule. The standard in-office days are Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday. Most Asanas have the option to work from home on Wednesdays. Working from home on Fridays depends on the type of work you do and the teams with which you partner. If you're interviewing for this role, your recruiter will share more about the in-office requirements.
What you'll achieve
Lead high-impact, cross-functional initiatives that span organizational boundaries. From IT infrastructure and AI adoption efforts to company-wide strategic initiatives in collaboration with Security, Product, Workplace, PeopleOps, Legal, and other partners.
Own your share of IT's process portfolio. You will fully own one or more highly visible IT processes and influence the development of all TPM processes. Throughout, you will maintain a focus on adaptation and continual improvement.
Run point on program communications. Keep stakeholders aligned, unblock teams, and build durable partnerships within and beyond IT.
Identify, manage, and mitigate risks and dependencies , ensuring alignment across key stakeholders to deliver successful outcomes.
Promote and evolve project management practice across IT. Create repeatable processes that leverage TPM best practices across the organization.
Drive adoption of policies, practices, and procedures across IT and Asana more broadly, through influence and tactful education rather than authority.
Bring a holistic view of the IT ecosystem to design and planning decisions, so solutions support our strategy and day to day operations.
Document and share knowledge so that processes and decisions are legible and repeatable by others, not dependent on any one person.
Help define how the TPM function operates. Partner with your manager to shape the team’s operating model, planning cadences, and processes.

6+ years of program management experience, with meaningful time working in or alongside IT organizations.
Proven ability to lead cross-functional teams through complex, ambiguous, multi-stakeholder work with only high-level direction. You are comfortable creating structure rather than waiting for it.
Strong grasp of business drivers, with the judgment to align processes to impact, design workable solutions, and implement improvements rather than defaulting to how it's always been done.
Comfortable operating with high autonomy across multiple concurrent workstreams, stakeholders, and timelines.
Excellent written and verbal communication. You enjoy distilling complex or ambiguous issues into actionable plans and can communicate clearly up, down, and across.
Demonstrates curiosity about AI tools and emerging technologies, with a willingness to learn and leverage them to enhance productivity, collaboration, or decision-making.
You know when to solve a problem yourself and when to bring in the right partner. Your title history matters less than how you think and how you work with people.
Experience across IT domains: IT Infrastructure, Identity & Access, Networking, Automations & Support.
PMP or ITIL certification.

Onboarding & Role Readiness
Design, launch, and continuously improve onboarding and readiness programs for the teams you support.
Partner with managers and SMEs to define what employees need to know and do, then build role-specific readiness roadmaps with clear learning, hands-on practice, and proficiency milestones.
Build reusable frameworks and tools that keep programs consistent while flexing to each team's needs.
Run structured check-ins through employees' first six months to reinforce learning, assess readiness, and close gaps.
Equip managers and SMEs with the guidance and tools they need to coach employees and validate proficiency on the job.
Ever-boarding & Employee Development
Build a plan for ongoing learning and skill development for the teams you support.
Partner with managers and SMEs to define role-specific skill and competency expectations.
Translate identified skill gaps into learning paths, refreshers, and practice opportunities.
Create engaging learning experiences — live sessions, shadowing, scenario practice, and recorded content.
Program Management & Continuous Improvement
Turn ambiguous team needs into clear, prioritized programs, and build iteratively.
Facilitate working sessions with managers, SMEs, and employees to define performance expectations.
Set success measures for learning effectiveness, proficiency, and time to readiness; use feedback and data to improve programs.
Use technology and AI-powered tools to make learning more personalized and efficient.

Bachelor's degree in a related field or equivalent practical experience.
3-5 years of experience in onboarding, employee enablement, learning and development, or program management.
Demonstrated experience taking at least one onboarding or readiness program from design through launch, adoption, and measurement.
Strong program management and facilitation skills, with the ability to move quickly from planning to execution.
Ability to build competency frameworks, learning paths, and clear documentation.
Strong analytical skills, with the ability to define success measures and use data to improve programs.
Experience with learning platforms, collaboration tools, or AI-powered tools is a plus.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Approach
Builder mindset — you're energized by creating something that doesn't exist yet and know how to turn ambiguity into action.
People-centered — you design around how employees actually learn, practice, work, and grow.
Creative — you challenge traditional approaches and find engaging ways to build knowledge, skills, and confidence.

Since we opened our doors in 2009, the world of commerce has evolved immensely, and so has Square. After enabling anyone to take payments and never miss a sale, we saw sellers stymied by disparate, outmoded products and tools that wouldn’t work together.
So we expanded into software and started building integrated, omnichannel solutions – to help sellers sell online, manage inventory, offer buy now, pay later functionality, book appointments, engage loyal buyers, and hire and pay staff.

Across it all, we’ve embedded financial services tools at the point of sale, so merchants can access a business loan and manage their cash flow in one place.

Afterpay furthers our goal to provide omnichannel tools that unlock meaningful value and growth, enabling sellers to capture the next generation shopper, increase order sizes, and compete at a larger scale.
Today, we are a partner to sellers of all sizes – large, enterprise-scale businesses with complex operations, sellers just starting, as well as merchants who began selling with Square and have grown larger over time. As our sellers grow, so do our solutions. There is a massive opportunity in front of us. We’re building a significant, meaningful, and lasting business, and we are helping sellers worldwide do the same.
Role
We’re looking for a Global Enablement Program Manager, who can bring to life the Afterpay and Cash App value propositions through our biggest channel: our people.

You will have the opportunity to build a global Afterpay and Cash App enablement & training strategy that educates, supports, and grows our go-to-market teams across Sales, Account Management, Partnerships and Customer Success.

You will own the program from the ground up, thinking about what matters most, how we best support our teams, and ultimately how we uplevel the skills of our people, to help them surpass their goals.

In this role, you will truly have the opportunity to manage a program that is mission critical to our organization's ability to scale, hit goals, and develop top talent.
This is a global role focused on North America, the UK and APAC. You may start the day sending out communications to the US team on recent business updates, followed by an end-of-day training session with the Australian team on a tool refresh.

s.h: You will develop a global enablement & training strategy that

Is a builder when it comes to AI, both building tools and supporting teams to ensure our teams are utilizing all the skills available to them, to be successful in their role.

This role is not just about tracking tickets; it is about shaping a new operating model, anticipating scale, and proving exponential ROI to executive stakeholders.

Strategic intake & triage
Manage the front door: Design, own, and refine a structured intake framework that evaluates incoming business requests and routes them to the appropriate technical track (e.g., technical consultation, rapid prototyping, or full production scaling).

Cross-functional leadership & governance
Strategic orchestration: Serve as the primary connective tissue between decentralized business units and the central engineering architecture team, operating in lockstep with the Senior Engineering Lead to ensure all operational, communication, and technical goals are met collectively.

Anticipate and orchestrate scale: Partner closely with engineering and business leads to forecast demand, proactively identifying when to seamlessly scale engineering capacity up or down to match evolving business roadmaps and team growth.

Executive communications & measurement
Evangelize program wins: Go beyond standard metrics by actively defining what "success" looks like across different business units. Craft and broadcast compelling success stories and operational wins across the entire enterprise to showcase tangible impact and drive ongoing program adoption.
Prove the value: Define, measure, and report on critical program KPIs, translating engineering velocity and cost consolidation into clear, executive-level ROI narratives.
Stakeholder alignment: Own the cross-functional communication strategy, ensuring transparent, predictable reporting across disparate teams, engineering leads, and C-suite stakeholders.
Operational readiness: Manage the critical path for program onboarding, ensuring all foundational technical dependencies, access permissions, and service level agreements (SLAs) are locked in for seamless execution.

Senior-level experience: 7+ years of experience in technical program management, product operations, product management, or technical account management, ideally within enterprise software, AI-enablement, or complex cloud environments.
Strategic agility: Proven ability to navigate highly matrixed, ambiguous enterprise organizations and build consensus among competing stakeholder priorities.
Process architecture: Deep experience building intake matrices, triage workflows, and operational playbooks from scratch.
Executive presence: Exceptional communication skills with the ability to translate deeply technical engineering challenges into clear business impacts for senior leadership.
Technical fluency: While you do not need to write code, you must possess a strong fundamental understanding of modern software development lifecycles, cloud architecture, and emerging AI technologies to effectively partner with Senior Engineers and TPMs.

Set a new pulse for healthcare!
We are looking for a Technical Program Manager to join the AI Lab team at Doctolib.
This is an opportunity to become the person who makes a new European clinical AI research lab work, from the inside, at an early stage.
The AI Lab is tackling long-horizon, high-stakes questions at the intersection of clinical AI, patient modelling, causal inference, calibration, privacy, and real-world evaluation , with access to one of Europe's largest longitudinal EHR datasets.
You will be the operational backbone of a rapidly growing lab, combining research scientists, data scientists, research engineers, PhD students, and research affiliates. Your role is to build and manage the processes, interfaces, and infrastructure that let researchers focus on research, within a product company operating at European scale, with real patients and clinicians on the other side of every decision.

s.h: Your responsibilities include but are not limited to
s.t:
Own the operating model. Design and run the Lab's core processes from the ground up: portfolio management, roadmap tracking, async documentation, and decision-making cadence. Where a task recurs, build a process.
Connect research and product. Understand both the Lab's projects and product teams' roadmaps well enough to propose concrete collaborations and follow them through. Lead recurring interfaces such as the bi-annual DS-Research workshop and monthly research on-sites, with agendas set in advance and pre-reads produced and read before the meeting.
Filter and triage inbound. Manage partnership proposals, collaboration requests, and internal asks: answering or redirecting most, escalating only what merits researcher time.
Track dependencies to resolution. Own operational blockers (data access, compute, contracts, academic collaboration administration) and drive them to closure with the relevant teams. For example: run a CIFRE application through the university, the doctoral school, and the ANRT fast enough that the intern starts the PhD without a gap.
Run hiring logistics. Interface with Talent Acquisition to keep the pipeline moving: scheduling, candidate communication, process documentation, scorecard templates. Researchers keep the assessments.
Map the ecosystem. Maintain a live view of labs, companies, and institutions working on adjacent topics; prepare targeting decisions for partnerships, workshops, and data challenges. Lead the first data challenge end to end, from platform setup and legal clearance to participant communication.
Move information in both directions. Collect what the Lab needs from product, data, medical, legal, and people teams; report the Lab's scientific outputs, programme health, and critical risks to the company with clarity and precision.
Before you read on: if you don't have the exact profile described below but feel this job description matches your skill set, we still encourage you to apply.

s.h: You'll be a great fit if you
s.t:
Have at least 5 years of experience in programme management, research operations, or a comparable high-complexity role, ideally within an AI, engineering, scientific, or product environment
Have a demonstrated ability to design and run processes from scratch, coordinate multiple workstreams across specialist teams, and hold a portfolio of priorities, dependencies, risks, and milestones with rigour
Are able to influence senior stakeholders and expert teams without formal authority, and follow unresolved items until they are resolved
Communicate with clarity and economy: you can make complex topics actionable for non-technical audiences and precise for technical ones
Have enough understanding of machine learning to follow research discussions, judge which requests merit researcher time, and translate the team's goals for the rest of the company; deep domain expertise can be learned on the job
Are fluent in English; working French is required, as academic-administration processes (CIFRE, ANRT, doctoral schools) run in French

s.h: It would be fantastic if you
s.t:
Have operated as Chief of Staff to a CTO, VP Engineering, Research Director, or Head of AI, or as a Research Operations Manager in an AI lab, university, hospital, or industrial research organisation
Are familiar with academic-industry collaborations, CIFRE, PhD programmes, grants, or data challenges
Have experience with clinical AI, healthtech, model evaluation, AI safety, privacy, or data governance

Company Description
We are Olsson. We engineer and design solutions that improve the world around us. As a company, we promise to always be responsive, transparent, and focused on results – for our people, our clients, and our company.
We’re a people-centric firm, so it’s no surprise our greatest asset is our people. The impact this creates is an environment that encourages our people to grow and be creative with their talents. This approach builds a culture that is uniquely Olsson. It allows us to grow our people as we grow our business. This, in turn, creates a lasting impact on the world around us.
Job Description
At Olsson, we are passionate about improving communities through expert engineering and design. Our people are our greatest asset, and we are committed to creating an environment where you can grow, lead, and make an impact.
Our Data Center team delivers multidisciplinary engineering and design services for some of the world's most innovative companies. These projects represent some of the largest and most complex infrastructure developments in the country, creating opportunities to solve challenging problems, collaborate across disciplines, and shape the facilities that support global connectivity.
We are seeking a Construction Administration Project Manager to help guide large-scale data center projects through the construction phase. In this role, you will connect design intent with field execution, coordinate across multidisciplinary teams, and help keep construction-phase decisions, documentation, and deliverables moving forward.

You will build trusted relationships with clients and project partners while supporting quality, safety, schedule, and successful project closeout. This role supports construction administration across data center projects and includes travel to project sites as needed for observations, meetings, and project coordination.

Serve as a primary connection between Olsson's design team, client representatives, contractors, consultants, and other project stakeholders during construction.
Coordinate construction-phase documentation, including requests for information, shop drawings, submittals, substitution requests, design packages, and related project records.
Review documentation for cross-discipline coordination, completeness, quality, and alignment with the design intent and contract documents.
Evaluate design changes and field conditions, coordinate technical input from the appropriate disciplines , and help assess potential effects on scope, schedule, and budget.
Lead or participate in project meetings, communicate decisions and action items, and follow through with the design team and project partners.
Track project progress, outstanding items, risks, and upcoming milestones while maintaining accurate and organized records.
Support project financial management through invoice coordination, change management, and monitoring of project budgets and schedules.
Conduct site observations as needed to monitor progress, identify potential deficiencies, and communicate findings to the appropriate parties .
Coordinate the resolution of technical and site-specific issues to help minimize rework, delays, and disruptions.
Support project closeout, including punch-list activities, final testing and commissioning coordination, record documents, and final deliverables.

Working collaboratively with others.
Having ownership in the work you do.
Using your talents to positively affect communities.

Bachelor's degree in Architecture , Engineering, Construction Management, or a related field. In lieu of a bachelor's degree, an associate degree with equivalent experience is required .
4+ years of experience within the Architecture, Engineering, and Construction (AEC) industry with increasing project responsibilities.
2+ years of project management, construction management, or construction administration experience, which may be concurrent with overall project experience.
Understanding of engineering and design terminology, construction processes, contracts, project financials, and relevant codes.
Strong communication , organization, time management, and problem-solving skills.
Ability to build effective relationships, navigate challenging conversations, and resolve issues across project teams.
Experience with Microsoft Office and construction management platforms. Experience with Procore, Autodesk Construction Cloud, Newforma, Smartsheet, or similar tools is beneficial.
Commitment to exceptional client service, quality, and safety.

The typical annual salary range for this role is as listed below. Compensation may vary based on geographic location, experience, and qualifications. Employees in this role may be eligible for our performance‑based bonus and merit increases.

Additional Information
Olsson specializes in engineering and design, client advisory services, planning, field services, and environmental. Improving the world has been our mindset from the very beginning, back when Olsson first opened for business in 1956. And it will be our mindset for years to come.

About Stripe
Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

Stripe’s Design organization builds the product and brand experiences that millions of businesses and developers rely on. We’re a cross-functional, global organization of product designers, content designers, design researchers, design systems engineers, motion designers, and design program specialists.
Our mission is to make economic infrastructure simple and accessible. Design plays a central role by making complex flows understandable, crafting clear product language, and building consistent systems that scale.
The Design Operations team leads Design’s business operations, runs cross-organizational programs, and builds the systems that help teams collaborate and produce high-quality work. Design Program Managers guide complex programs through the design lifecycle and apply design thinking to our operating model. They prototype and iterate on how our team works.
We’re looking for a Design Program Manager to partner with the Research team. This full-time role reports to the Head of Design Operations.

Lead and build programs for the Research organization. Develop and implement processes and resources that support impactful research and scale the use of user insights across Stripe.
Improve our operating model and processes, including automating tasks, improving workflows, and developing repeatable methodologies. Measure the impact of these changes.

Experis ist ein global führender Anbieter im Bereich IT Professional Resourcing, Feststellenvermittlung, Projektdienstleistungen und Managed Services. Mit über 25 Jahren Erfahrung in der Schweiz und Standorten in Zürich, Basel und Genf verbinden wir IT-Spezialisten mit führenden Unternehmen.
**​**
Als erfahrener Software Project Manager übernimmst du die Verantwortung für externe Kundenprojekte im Softwareumfeld – von der Initialisierung über die Planung und Umsetzung bis hin zur erfolgreichen Einführung. Du schaffst Klarheit über Ziele, Scope, Budget, Termine, Prioritäten, Risiken und nächste Schritte und sorgst dafür, dass komplexe Vorhaben strukturiert, verbindlich und lösungsorientiert vorankommen.
Du bist die zentrale Ansprechperson für Kunden und interne Stakeholder während der Projektphase. Die Umsetzung stimmst du eng mit den Product Ownern ab, die als zentrale Schnittstelle zu den Entwicklungsteams agieren. Dabei behältst du jederzeit den Überblick über Kosten, Termine und Leistungsumfang, erkennst Abweichungen frühzeitig und klärst diese transparent und lösungsorientiert mit dem Kunden.
**Bei uns wirst du:**
· anspruchsvolle Softwareprojekte mit Kunden eigenverantwortlich planen, steuern und erfolgreich zur Einführung bringen
· als zentrale Ansprechperson für Kunden, Stakeholder, Product Owner und interne Fachbereiche agieren
· Projektziele, Scope, Budget, Termine, Prioritäten, Risiken und Abhängigkeiten aktiv managen
· Change Requests, Weiterentwicklungen und neue Anforderungen strukturiert aufnehmen, bewerten und in die Projekt- und Budgetplanung integrieren
· für klare Entscheidungen, verbindliche nächste Schritte und eine saubere Übergabe in den laufenden Service sorgen
**Du kennst dich unter anderem aus mit:**
· Projektleitung im Softwareumfeld
· Stakeholder-, Priorisierungs- und Risikomanagement
· Scope-, Budget-, Termin- und Erwartungsmanagement
· Requirements Engineering, Lösungsdesign und Change Management auf Steuerungs- und Koordinationsebene
· technischen Grundlagen der Softwareentwicklung sowie der Zusammenarbeit mit Product Ownern und Fachbereichen
**Das bringst du mit:**
· fundierte Erfahrung in der Leitung von Softwareprojekten mit externen Kunden
· die Fähigkeit, komplexe Projektkontexte souverän zu strukturieren und mehrere Themen parallel zu führen
· ein hohes Mass an Verbindlichkeit, Verantwortungsbewusstsein und Durchsetzungsfähigkeit
· ein gutes Gespür für Prioritäten, Risiken, Qualität, Kundenbedürfnisse und realistische Planung

s.h: So läuft der Bewerbungsprozess bei uns ab
s.t:
Schritt 1: Online Bewerbung
Reiche deine Bewerbungsunterlagen online über unser Jobportal ein. Damit wir deine Unterlagen weiterbearbeiten können, musst du ein Login erstellen. Nachdem du deine Bewerbung eingereicht hast, erhältst du eine Bestätigung. Wir beurteilen jede Bewerbung individuell anhand der Kriterien im Stelleninserat. Das braucht manchmal etwas Zeit. Wenn deine Bewerbung passt, kontaktieren wir dich für ein erstes Gespräch.
Schritt 2: Gespräche
Im Vorstellungsgespräch - telefonisch, vor Ort oder online - möchten wir dich kennenlernen. Wir überprüfen, ob deine Erwartungen an die Stelle mit unseren übereinstimmen, welche Erfahrungen und Fähigkeiten du mitbringst, ob dich unsere Kultur anspricht und wie du ins Team passt. Bei beidseitigem Interesse und je nach Stelle finden mehrere Gespräche statt. Alle deine Fragen zur Stelle, zum Team oder zu den Anstellungsbedingungen sind immer willkommen.
Schritt 3: Weitere Schritte im Prozess
Je nach Stelle vereinbaren wir einen Probe- oder Schnuppertag, stellen dir eine fachliche Aufgabe, organisieren ein Treffen mit dem Team oder laden zu einem Assessment ein. In der Regel gehören auch Referenzauskünfte zu unserem Bewerbungsablauf. Über alle Schritte im Prozess wirst du transparent informiert.
Schritt 4: Bewerbungsentscheid
Du bist von uns überzeugt und wir von dir? Nach einer mündlichen Zusage erhältst du eine Bestätigung, die Vertragsunterlagen und Informationen, wie es bis zum Stellenantritt weitergeht. Es hat nicht geklappt? Wir freuen uns, wenn du dich trotz Absage auf andere spannende Stellen bewirbst.

**About Syngenta**
At Syngenta Crop Protection, we're pioneering solutions that safeguard global food security while championing sustainable agriculture. As a world market leader headquartered in Switzerland, we empower farmers with innovative crop protection technologies that defend against nature's toughest challenges.

We unite advanced science with digital solutions to develop intelligent crop protection that maximizes yields while minimizing environmental impact.

Join our mission of revolutionizing plant protection from seed to harvest. **Syngenta has been ranked as a-top employer-by Science Magazine and it has been awarded with the "Friendly Work Space" label to all its Swiss sites.**
## Job Description ##
At Syngenta, our goal is to build the most collaborative and trustworthy team in agriculture, providing top-quality seeds and innovative crop protection solutions that improve farmers' success. To support this mission, we are seeking a **Global Environmental Technology Lead**. This is a hybrid role based primarily in Muttenz, Switzerland, though Monthey can also be considered.
As Global Environmental Technology Lead, you will shape how Production & Supply identifies, develops and deploys the technologies that reduce environmental impact while protecting operational performance and our license to operate.

This is a high-impact global role for an accomplished scientist or engineer who can move confidently between technical depth, strategic direction and practical implementation. You will connect manufacturing sites, process development, environmental specialists and external partners to turn complex environmental challenges into scalable solutions.

* Set the global environmental technology strategy across waste, wastewater, air emissions, vent treatment, recovery and recycling, informed by Best Available Techniques (BAT).
* Identify, assess and mature emerging technologies, taking opportunities from laboratory and pilot-scale evidence through to robust manufacturing application.
* Partner with global and local manufacturing teams to solve critical environmental challenges, improve site performance and safeguard license to operate.
* Provide technical leadership and independent challenge for environmental projects, assessing feasibility, environmental benefit, risk, operability and cost.
* Influence product and process choices early by evaluating waste streams, especially wastewater, during active-ingredient process development.
* Develop practical, high-value solutions that reduce impacts to air, water and land across existing products and manufacturing sites.
* Build and lead a connected global environmental technology community spanning Technology & Engineering, Production & Supply, Environmental Managers, process development teams and external experts.
* Grow internal capabilities through technical coaching, knowledge exchange, training, literature reviews and partnerships with suppliers, consultants and technology providers.
* Translate complex environmental science and regulation into clear choices and decisive action for technical and business stakeholders.

* Master-s degree, or equivalent, in Chemistry, Chemical Process Engineering or a related discipline.
* Ideally 10+ years- experience in industrial chemical operations and/or process development.
* Demonstrated expertise in environmental technologies and a practical understanding of environmental legislation.
* Able to remain focused, resilient and effective in a fast-paced, high-pressure environment.
* Strong knowledge of waste, wastewater, emissions, recovery and recycling technologies.
* Solid grounding in organic and inorganic chemistry, chemical processes and process engineering; agrochemical production knowledge is an advantage.
* Working knowledge of environmental toxicity, chemical bio-transformation and environmental risk assessment.
* Proven ability to lead teams or workstreams in project, departmental or matrix environments.
* Experience in project and change management, with resilience in ambiguous environments.
* Strong analytical, conceptual, organisational and negotiation skills.
* Clear communication and stakeholder-influencing skills at all levels.
* Experience working across multicultural, multinational teams, with a recognised record of technical delivery.
* Fluent business English; French is highly advantageous.

* The opportunity to make a difference to process safety, both within Syngenta-s global operations, and in shaping safety legislation and culture worldwide
* A super working environment with an open culture and diverse workforce where new ideas are always welcome

* Learning culture (Together we Grow) and wide range of training options

Gestalten Sie mit uns die Zukunft der Sozialberatung
Die Sozialberatung ist eines der zentralen Angebote von Pro Senectute Kanton Luzern. Rund 25 Mitarbeitende an den Standorten Luzern, Emmen und Willisau sowie bei der Infostelle Demenz beraten und begleiten ältere Menschen und ihre Angehörigen in unterschiedlichen Lebenssituationen.

* Sie führen den Bereich Sozialberatung und entwickeln ihn mit Blick auf gesellschaftliche Veränderungen und die zukünftigen Bedürfnisse älterer Menschen und ihrer Angehörigen gemeinsam mit den Mitarbeitenden weiter.

* Als Mitglied der Geschäftsleitung tragen Sie Mitverantwortung für die Gesamtorganisation und wirken bei strategischen Fragestellungen, Organisationsentwicklungen und bereichsübergreifenden Projekten mit.
Das bringen Sie mit

* Eine Weiterbildung in Führung, Management oder Organisationsentwicklung
* Mehrjährige Berufs- und Führungserfahrung, vorzugsweise im Sozial-, Gesundheits- oder Non-Profit-Bereich
* Freude, Menschen zu führen, Mitarbeitende zu entwickeln und gemeinsam Veränderungen zu gestalten
* Die Fähigkeit, fachliche, personelle und betriebswirtschaftliche Fragestellungen miteinander zu verbinden

* Eine überzeugende Kommunikation und ein sicheres Auftreten gegenüber Mitarbeitenden, Behörden, Gemeinden und weiteren Partnerorganisationen
* Interesse an gesellschaftlichen und sozialpolitischen Fragestellungen rund um das Alter
* Eine selbständige, verantwortungsbewusste und lösungsorientierte Arbeitsweise

Sie bewegen sich in einem vielseitigen Umfeld an der Schnittstelle zwischen Sozialer Arbeit, Führung, Organisationsentwicklung und der Zusammenarbeit mit Gemeinden, Behörden und Fachorganisationen.

JUUL Labs is seeking a multifunctional Manufacturing Operations Program Manager to join our Global Supply Chain team. This hybrid role bridges day-to-day contract manufacturing execution with strategic, end-to-end supply chain management.
The mission of this role is to ensure we build products at the right speed (time to market), right price (fully burdened cost), right capacity, and right flexibility to meet the company's growth needs. Acting as a critical operational liaison, you will oversee the complete lifecycle of new and existing products across our global supplier network.
Looking for Candidate in Region who can travel to manufacturing site in Cookeville, TN as needed.

Time to Market & Operational Execution
Launch Optimization: Optimize product supply chains for speed to successfully meet market demand and product launch timelines.
Lead Time Reduction: Work closely with product development and manufacturing teams to minimize lead times while maintaining strict quality standards.
Day-to-Day Oversight: Interface daily with suppliers to manage operational execution, focusing heavily on On-Time Delivery (OTD), Overall Operational Effectiveness (OOE), and forecast execution.
Cost Management & Financial Acumen
Fully Burdened Cost Tracking: Manage total product supply chain costs to ensure the fully burdened price (including material, labor, overhead, and logistics) directly aligns with corporate profitability margins.
Should-Cost Strategy: Partner with finance and engineering to build aggressive should-costs and clear capital expenditure forecasts.
Commercial Negotiations: Negotiate with key suppliers to secure favorable pricing, tooling/equipment budgets, and business terms without compromising product quality.
Capacity Planning, Flexibility & Scalability
Constraint Mitigation: Evaluate production constraints and manage global manufacturing capacity to seamlessly support current volumes and future product roadmaps.
Ramp & Scale Planning: Collaborate with manufacturing partners on staffing, facility foot printing, and equipment allocation to ensure infrastructure is scalable for company growth.
Adaptability: Implement flexible supply chain strategies capable of responding rapidly to market fluctuations, operational bottlenecks, and demand shifts.
Supplier Relationship & Risk Management
Strategic Alignment: Build, evaluate, and maintain relationships with critical contract manufacturers and component vendors to align them with JUUL's operational targets.
Contingency Planning: Anticipate vulnerabilities and draft proactive business continuity plans to mitigate risks associated with vendor performance, geopolitical fluctuations, and macro supply disruptions.
Performance Quality: Establish metric scorecards and Clear to Build (CTB) tracking to eliminate post-ramp qualifications and unexpected disruptions.
Cross-Functional Leadership & Continuous Improvement
Primary Liaison: Act as the primary champion and operational advocate across engineering, quality, product management, logistics, and finance.
Process Excellence: Utilize KPIs to actively monitor supply chain performance, using a data-driven "sixth sense" to spark continuous improvement, process modifications, and cost-saving loops.

Every contact that reaches a customer support agent, and every credit issued to customers, represents a defect somewhere in our system. This role exists to help find those defects, trace them to their source, and work with the teams responsible to eliminate them at a systemic level.
This is a high impact senior program management role within the EMEA Customer Experience organisation, reporting to the Director of Defect Elimination and Customer Experience. The Senior Program Manager is accountable for turning customer experience signals from Wolt and/or Deliveroo markets into clear, actionable insight, and for driving the resulting fixes through to resolution with partner teams.
What you’ll be doing
You will own the delivery of the defect elimination program across EMEA, including application of the defect driver taxonomy to identify where defect rate concentrates, and where customer outcomes are worst. You will build a clear, prioritised list of issues for partner teams to work through.
You will represent the voice of the customer in the rooms where decisions get made about your markets. That means preparing and presenting data in product reviews, weekly/monthly business reviews and planning sessions, so the cost of poor customer experience is concrete and attributable, and so partner teams understand what is being asked of them and why.
You will build working relationships with partner teams in engineering, marketplace operations, courier operations, and finance, and you will track the fixes they commit to through to completion. You will feed results back into the program so everyone can see what worked, and to ensure defects are eliminated for good.
You will maintain and improve the data infrastructure and reporting that underpins this work, ensuring customer experience insights are credible, available and actionable.
Our humble expectations
The right person for this role has spent time inside a large-scale customer experience or operations function, and has direct experience translating customer defects through identification, root cause analysis and resolution. They are comfortable working with imperfect data, and they know how to build a credible case when the evidence is directional rather than conclusive.
Strong analytical instincts are essential. This person needs to know what questions to ask of the data and whether the answers make sense. Prior exposure to a successful voice of the customer (VoC) program is critical.
There is a meaningful cross-functional dimension to the role. This person will spend real time getting other teams to prioritise work that benefits the customer but may compete with other priorities. That requires good judgement, clear communication, and the ability to build trust quickly with people outside their reporting line.
The role also requires the ability to drive results in a dynamic and ambiguous landscape. The right person will combine introducing structure and rigor, while being agile and responsive to changing priorities and emerging issues.
This is a high impact and high visibility role, with the opportunity to interact with stakeholders and teams across the full customer lifecycle. The role will also span across 40 EMEA Roo & Wolt markets, meaning there is an opportunity to drive financial and customer experience results at scale.
Next steps
You will first meet with our Talent Acquisition team to understand role and company fit. Then, you will meet with the Hiring Manager who will talk through your relevant experience and ask you competency based questions that assess your suitability for the role.

The third stage is an assignment, where you will be given a business problem to think through, and present back to the team. If successful, there may be a final conversation with a more senior stakeholder. Throughout all stages, you will have plenty of opportunities to ask any questions about the role, team or company.
Our Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion
We’re committed to growing and empowering a more inclusive community within our company, industry, and cities. That’s why we hire and cultivate diverse teams of people from all backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We believe that true innovation happens when everyone has room at the table and the tools, resources, and opportunity to excel.

Every contact that reaches a customer support agent, and every credit issued to customers, represents a defect somewhere in our system. This role exists to help find those defects, trace them to their source, and work with the teams responsible to eliminate them at a systemic level.
This is a high impact senior program management role within the EMEA Customer Experience organisation, reporting to the Director of Defect Elimination and Customer Experience. The Senior Program Manager is accountable for turning customer experience signals from Wolt and/or Deliveroo markets into clear, actionable insight, and for driving the resulting fixes through to resolution with partner teams.
What you'll be doing
You will own the delivery of the defect elimination program across EMEA, including application of the defect driver taxonomy to identify where defect rate concentrates, and where customer outcomes are worst. You will build a clear, prioritised list of issues for partner teams to work through.
You will represent the voice of the customer in the rooms where decisions get made about your markets. That means preparing and presenting data in product reviews, weekly/monthly business reviews and planning sessions, so the cost of poor customer experience is concrete and attributable, and so partner teams understand what is being asked of them and why.
You will build working relationships with partner teams in engineering, marketplace operations, courier operations, and finance, and you will track the fixes they commit to through to completion. You will feed results back into the program so everyone can see what worked, and to ensure defects are eliminated for good.
You will maintain and improve the data infrastructure and reporting that underpins this work, ensuring customer experience insights are credible, available and actionable.
Our humble expectations
The right person for this role has spent time inside a large-scale customer experience or operations function, and has direct experience translating customer defects through identification, root cause analysis and resolution. They are comfortable working with imperfect data, and they know how to build a credible case when the evidence is directional rather than conclusive.
Strong analytical instincts are essential. This person needs to know what questions to ask of the data and whether the answers make sense. Prior exposure to a successful voice of the customer (VoC) program is critical.
There is a meaningful cross-functional dimension to the role. This person will spend real time getting other teams to prioritise work that benefits the customer but may compete with other priorities. That requires good judgement, clear communication, and the ability to build trust quickly with people outside their reporting line.
The role also requires the ability to drive results in a dynamic and ambiguous landscape. The right person will combine introducing structure and rigor, while being agile and responsive to changing priorities and emerging issues.
This is a high impact and high visibility role, with the opportunity to interact with stakeholders and teams across the full customer lifecycle. The role will also span across 40 EMEA Roo & Wolt markets, meaning there is an opportunity to drive financial and customer experience results at scale.
Next steps
You will first meet with our Talent Acquisition team to understand role and company fit. Then, you will meet with the Hiring Manager who will talk through your relevant experience and ask you competency based questions that assess your suitability for the role.

The third stage is an assignment, where you will be given a business problem to think through, and present back to the team. If successful, there may be a final conversation with a more senior stakeholder. Throughout all stages, you will have plenty of opportunities to ask any questions about the role, team or company.
Our Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion
We're committed to growing and empowering a more inclusive community within our company, industry, and cities. That's why we hire and cultivate diverse teams of people from all backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We believe that true innovation happens when everyone has room at the table and the tools, resources, and opportunity to excel.

Axon Community Connect enables public safety agencies to build voluntary, policy-based partnerships with businesses and community members. As the PSO Program Manager, Community Connect, you will lead the operational health and scalable execution of the Community Connect program across Axon’s U.S. customer base and growing international footprint.
You will establish the operating discipline that enables Program Coordinators to deliver consistent agency outcomes. You will serve as a program-level escalation resource, coordinating with Professional Services, Product, Engineering, Support, Sales, and Finance to remove blockers and drive resolution. You will also provide consultative support for hardware deployment readiness, remote hardware configuration and activation, connectivity, and camera integration requirements.
Your work will enable agencies to launch and sustain Community Connect programs that extend operational visibility, strengthen community participation, and scale responsibly without compromising privacy or the customer experience.

Job Description
Join Olsson’s Federal Engineering & Design Team as a Project Manager II, where you will support the delivery of impactful infrastructure projects for federal clients. In this role, you will work with multidisciplinary teams to plan, design, and support construction for mission-critical facilities for military bases, VA campuses, and other government agencies. These projects require technical excellence, regulatory accuracy, and strong collaboration.
As a Project Manager II, you will oversee project deliverables for small- to mid-sized projects within a single discipline or defined area, as well as low-risk multidisciplinary projects, or provide support on larger project teams. You will be involved throughout the full project life cycle, managing scope, schedule, budget, and quality to ensure projects are completed on time and within established parameters.
You will collaborate closely with internal teams and federal stakeholders to support compliance with UFC, DoD, VA, and other applicable federal standards. From early concept development through project delivery, you will help guide teams toward practical, high-quality engineering and design solutions that meet client needs.
In addition, you will contribute to proposal development and support continuous improvement efforts that enhance our federal design capabilities. This role offers the opportunity to support projects that serve national interests while building your project management expertise within a collaborative team environment.

A minimum of six years of project experience in the Architecture, Engineering, or Construction industry with increasing responsibility.
Proven success managing multidisciplinary teams and delivering federal projects for agencies such as DoD and VA.
Strong understanding of federal design standards, acquisition processes, contract requirements, and project financials.
Exceptional leadership, communication, and organizational skills.
High-level proficiency in client service, negotiation, and decision-making.
Ability to navigate complex regulatory environments with precision and integrity.
Demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities in fast-paced settings and exceed client expectations.
Strong interpersonal skills and a commitment to mentoring and team development.
Deep understanding of consulting business operations and a drive to contribute to firm-wide success.

Assemble and lead federal design teams, aligning technical expertise with project goals and applicable federal requirements.
Define and communicate project scope in coordination with technical teams and develop project schedules and budgets in collaboration with clients and contractors.
Develop and manage project budgets, review costs, and track financial performance to ensure adherence to planned budgets, client satisfaction, and overall project success.
Serve as the primary point of contact for clients and stakeholders, maintaining alignment on expectations, performance, and compliance with UFC, DoD, VA, and other applicable federal standards.
Identify potential risks, scope changes, and additional costs, and implement mitigation strategies to minimize financial and operational impacts.
Manage contracts, change orders, and support contract negotiations, including coordination with technical disciplines on billing and contract requirements.
Develop and implement quality management and quality assurance plans to ensure projects meet client expectations and firm standards.
Plan, organize, and lead routine project meetings with clients and project teams to support communication, alignment, and progress tracking.
Oversee the preparation, delivery, and maintenance of project documentation, including design plans, specifications, correspondence, and performance records.

Contribute to projects that serve national interests and make a difference in communities.
Enjoy flexible work arrangements, including remote options, to support your work-life balance.
Thrive in a supportive culture that values professional development and teamwork.
At Olsson, your expertise drives progress on projects that matter. If you’re passionate about federal civil engineering and ready to elevate your career, we want to hear from you.

Olsson specializes in engineering and design, client advisory services, planning, field services, and environmental. Improving the world has been our mindset from the very beginning, back when Olsson first opened for business in 1956. And it will be our mindset for years to come.

### Process and Tooling Team Introduction ###
Cloud Interconnection & Acquisition | Network Fiber
### Who We Are ###
We are the Process and Tooling team supporting CIA Network Fiber, focused on simplifying how teams plan, source, deliver, and manage fiber work across regions. Our team partners closely with sourcing, delivery, engineering, operations, GIS, and regional stakeholders to turn complex workflows into clear, scalable processes and practical tooling solutions.

Our mission is to create consistent, efficient, and repeatable ways of working that reduce manual effort, improve visibility, and help teams move fiber programs forward with greater speed and confidence. We focus on standardizing processes, improving tool adoption, clarifying ownership, and enabling better decision-making through reliable data and well-defined workflows.

We are seeking a Technical Program Manager to drive process & tooling optimization and automation, primarily focused on AI driven improvements to accelerate transformation across global cloud and network operations.
This role sits at the intersection of business process optimization, AI adoption, tooling, and intelligent automation engineering. You will lead the identification, development, and scaling of AI powered capabilities, process improvement and tooling requirements -embedding Copilot, automation, and predictive analytics into operational workflows to improve speed to market, data quality, cost efficiency, and decision making.
The ideal candidate thrives in complex, matrixed environments, can move seamlessly between strategy and execution, and delivers measurable impact through responsible, scalable AI solutions.
**Key Responsibilities - Process Optimization, Tooling & Automation with Focus on AI**
* Map, analyze, and optimize end-to-end operational processes across network sourcing, inventory, planning, fiber lifecycle, and engineering workflows.
* Eliminate friction, standardize practices, and reduce cycle times using AI enabled automation.
* Partner with CIA and our partner teams to ensure integrated, scalable tooling solutions aligned to business priorities.
**AI, Data & System Integration**
* Strengthen data quality, interoperability, and automation across network and operational tools.
* Enable AI powered data cleansing, reconciliation, forecasting, and predictive modeling.
* Support system modernization initiatives to ensure platforms are AI-ready and interoperable.
* Act as a connector between business owners, engineering teams, and AI/data science resources.
* Design, develop, and deploy agents and agent flows that support operational workflows.
* Translate repeatable patterns into scalable, automated solutions.
* Ensure AI solutions are reliable, maintainable, secure, and aligned with engineering best practices.
* Integrate automation solutions with existing systems and Microsoft platforms.
* Support deployment, monitoring, and continuous improvement of AI and automation solutions in production environments.
* Contribute to technical documentation, operational readiness, and knowledge sharing.
* Lead AI change management efforts to drive AI literacy and adoption across teams.
* Develop training, documentation, and communications that accelerate responsible AI usage.
* Foster an AI first, growth mindset culture grounded in Microsoft-s Responsible AI principles, security, and governance standards.

* Bachelor-s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Data, Telecommunications, Finance, or related field AND some experience in these fields OR equivalent experience
* Some experience managing cross-functional and/or cross-team projects

* Some experience in cloud, data center, or large-scale network environments.
* Solid experience in program management, process improvement, automation, or operations.
* Hands-on experience with AI tools, including Copilot and/or Copilot Studio.
* Experience developing automation or analytics solutions using Python or similar languages.
* Strong understanding of network or infrastructure lifecycles.
* Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office, including Excel with financial or operational data.
* Proven ability to influence across highly matrixed organizations.
* Strong analytical mindset with the ability to translate data into actionable insights.
* Excellent communication, documentation, and stakeholder management skills.

* Familiarity with Azure services, Kusto queries, APIs, or enterprise data platforms.
* Experience with Lean, Six Sigma, or value-stream mapping.

Über uns
Die Fachstelle für Gleichstellung ist das Kompetenzzentrum für die rechtliche und tatsächliche Gleichstellung von Frauen und Männern sowie von Lesben, Schwulen, Bisexuellen, trans und intergeschlechtlichen Menschen in der Stadt Zürich. Sie ist Anlaufstelle für die Bevölkerung und Organisationen der Stadt Zürich einerseits und für die Mitarbeitenden der Zürcher Stadtverwaltung andererseits. Die Fachstelle gehört zum Präsidialdepartement und ist dem Stadtpräsidium direkt unterstellt.
